title.en: Volume 121 Biographies 8: Subutai, Anzhu'er, Weida'er, Boluohuan, Chaosi,
title.raw: 卷一百二十一 列傳第八: 速不台 按竺邇 畏答兒 博羅歡 抄思 Volume 121 Biographies 8: Subutai, Anzhu'er, Weida'er, Boluohuan, Chaosi,

sentences.zh: 速不臺

translations.literal: Subutai
translations.idiomatic: Subutai

sentences.zh: 速不臺，蒙古兀良合人。

translations.literal: Subutai was a Mongol of the Uriankhai.
translations.idiomatic: Subutai was a Mongol of the Uriankhai clan.

sentences.zh: 其先世獵於斡難河上，遇敦必乃皇帝，因相結納，至太祖時，已五世矣。

translations.literal: His ancestors hunted on the Onon River, met Emperor Dombina, and formed a bond; by the time of the Founder it had already been five generations.
translations.idiomatic: His forebears had hunted along the Onon River and entered into alliance with Emperor Dombina; by the Founder’s day the bond had already spanned five generations.

sentences.zh: 捏里必者生孛忽都，眾目為折里麻。

translations.literal: Nielibi begot Bükütu, whom the multitude regarded as Jelme.
translations.idiomatic: Nielibi had a son named Bükütu, whom people hailed as Jelme—a man of counsel.

sentences.zh: 折里麻者，漢言有謀略人也。

translations.literal: Jelme means in Chinese ‘a man of stratagem.’
translations.idiomatic: Jelme, in Chinese parlance, meant ‘a man of strategy.’

sentences.zh: 三世孫合赤溫，生哈班。

translations.literal: The third-generation descendant Qachi’un begot Qaban.
translations.idiomatic: Three generations later Qachi’un was born, and he in turn fathered Qaban.

sentences.zh: 哈班二子，長忽魯渾，次速不臺，俱驍勇善騎射。

translations.literal: Qaban had two sons: the elder Qorqunas, the younger Subutai; both were valiant and skilled in riding and archery.
translations.idiomatic: Qaban had two sons—the elder Qorqunas and the younger Subutai—both fierce horsemen and expert archers.

sentences.zh: 太祖在班朱尼河時，哈班嘗驅群羊以進，遇盜，被執。

translations.literal: When the Founder was at the Baljuna River, Qaban once drove a flock of sheep to present them and met bandits who seized him.
translations.idiomatic: While the Founder was encamped on the Baljuna River, Qaban once drove a flock of sheep to the camp as tribute; bandits waylaid him and took him captive.

sentences.zh: 忽魯渾與速不臺繼至，以槍剌之，人馬皆倒，余黨逸去，遂免父難，羊得達於行在所。

translations.literal: Qorqunas and Subutai came after, stabbed with spears, and men and horses all fell; the rest fled, thus freeing their father from peril, and the sheep reached the imperial encampment.
translations.idiomatic: Qorqunas and Subutai came up behind them, speared the raiders, and brought down men and horses alike; the rest scattered, their father was saved, and the flock reached the imperial camp.

sentences.zh: 忽魯渾以百戶從帝與乃蠻部主戰於長城之南，忽魯渾射卻之，其眾奔闊赤檀山而潰。

translations.literal: Qorqunas, as a centurion, followed the Emperor to fight the Naiman chieftain south of the Long Wall; Qorqunas shot and repelled him, and his host fled in rout toward Kuochitan Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: Serving as a centurion, Qorqunas followed the Emperor against the Naiman chieftain south of the Long Wall; he drove the enemy back with his bow, and the Naiman forces broke and fled toward Kuochitan Mountain.

sentences.zh: 速不臺以質子事帝，為百戶。

translations.literal: Subutai served the Emperor as a hostage-prince and became a centurion.
translations.idiomatic: Subutai served the Founder as a hostage in the imperial household and was made a centurion.

sentences.zh: 歲壬申，攻金桓州，先登，拔其城。

translations.literal: In the year renshen he attacked the Jin Huanzhou, was first to ascend, and captured the city.
translations.idiomatic: In the renshen year he assaulted the Jin fortress of Huanzhou, was first over the wall, and took the city.

sentences.zh: 帝命賜金帛一車。

translations.literal: The Emperor ordered that he be given a cartload of gold and silks.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor rewarded him with a cartload of gold and silks.

sentences.zh: 滅裏吉部強盛不附，丙子，帝會諸將於禿兀剌河之黑林，問：「誰能為我征滅裏吉者？」

translations.literal: The Merkit tribe was powerful and would not submit; in bingzi the Emperor assembled the generals at Heilin on the Tuwula River and asked, ‘Who can campaign against the Merkit for me?’
translations.idiomatic: The Merkit were strong and refused allegiance; in the bingzi year the Founder gathered his generals at Heilin on the Tuwula River and asked, “Who will march against the Merkit for me?”

sentences.zh: 速不臺請行，帝壯而許之。

translations.literal: Subutai requested to go; the Emperor approved his spirit and granted it.
translations.idiomatic: Subutai volunteered for the mission; impressed by his spirit, the Founder assented.

sentences.zh: 乃選裨將阿裏出領百人先行，覘其虛實。

translations.literal: He then chose the lieutenant-general Alchu to lead a hundred men ahead to reconnoiter their strength.
translations.idiomatic: He chose the lieutenant Alchu to take a hundred men ahead and scout the enemy’s strength.

sentences.zh: 速不臺繼進。

translations.literal: Subutai advanced after.
translations.idiomatic: Subutai followed with the main force.

sentences.zh: 速不臺戒阿裏出曰：「汝止宿，必載嬰兒具以行，去則遺之，使若挈家而逃者。」

translations.literal: Subutai admonished Alchu, saying, ‘When you halt for the night, you must carry infant gear on the march; when you leave, abandon it, so that it seems as if families are fleeing.’
translations.idiomatic: Subutai instructed Alchu: “Whenever you make camp, take along child-care gear on the march; when you move on, leave it behind, as though whole families were fleeing in panic.”

sentences.zh: 滅裏吉見之，果以為逃者，遂不為備。

translations.literal: The Merkit saw this and indeed took them for fugitives, and therefore made no preparations.
translations.idiomatic: The Merkit saw the discarded gear, took it for proof of a rout, and let down their guard.

sentences.zh: 己卯，大軍至蟾河，與滅裏吉遇，一戰而獲其二將，盡降其眾。

translations.literal: In jimao the great army reached the Chan River, encountered the Merkit, and in one battle captured two of their generals and wholly subdued their host.
translations.idiomatic: In the jimao year the main army reached the Chan River, met the Merkit, and in a single engagement took two of their commanders captive and brought the whole tribe to submission.

sentences.zh: 其部主霍都奔欽察，速不臺追之，與欽察戰於玉峪，敗之。

translations.literal: Their chieftain Qoto fled to the Qipchaq; Subutai pursued, fought the Qipchaq at Yuyu, and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: Their chief Qoto fled to the Qipchaq; Subutai pursued him, met the Qipchaq at Yuyu, and routed them.

sentences.zh: 壬午，帝征回回國，其主滅裏委國而去。

translations.literal: In renwu the Emperor campaigned against the Muslim realm; its lord Muhammad abandoned the state and fled.
translations.idiomatic: In the renwu year the Founder marched against the Khwarazmian realm; Sultan Muhammad abandoned his kingdom and fled.

sentences.zh: 命速不臺與只別追之，及於灰裏河，只別戰不利，速不臺駐軍河東，戒其眾人爇三炬以張軍勢，其王夜遁。

translations.literal: He ordered Subutai and Jebe to pursue; they reached the Huili River. Jebe’s battle went ill; Subutai encamped east of the river and ordered his men to light three beacon-fires to magnify the army’s appearance, and the king fled by night.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered Subutai and Jebe to pursue. At the Huili River Jebe’s wing fared badly; Subutai halted east of the river and had his men light three signal fires to swell the apparent strength of the host, and the sultan slipped away under cover of night.

sentences.zh: 復命統兵萬人由不罕川必裏罕城追之，凡所經歷，皆無水之地。

translations.literal: He was again ordered to command ten thousand men and pursue by way of the Buhan River and the city of Bukhara; everywhere they passed was waterless land.
translations.idiomatic: He was again placed at the head of ten thousand men and sent in pursuit by way of the Buhan valley and Bukhara; the whole route lay through waterless wastes.

sentences.zh: 既度川，先發千人為遊騎，繼以大軍晝夜兼行。

translations.literal: Having crossed the river, he first sent a thousand as scouting cavalry, then followed with the main army marching day and night without rest.
translations.idiomatic: Once across the river he sent a thousand light horse ahead as scouts, then pressed on with the main force day and night without halt.

sentences.zh: 比至，滅裏逃入海，不月餘，病死，盡獲其所棄珍寶以獻。

translations.literal: By the time they arrived, Muhammad had fled onto the sea; within little more than a month he died of illness, and they wholly seized the treasures he had abandoned and presented them.
translations.idiomatic: When they arrived Muhammad had taken to the sea; within a month he died of sickness, and they recovered all the treasure he had abandoned and presented it to the court.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「速不臺枕幹血戰，為我家宣勞，朕甚嘉之。」

translations.literal: The Emperor said, ‘Subutai has fought with his head on the saddle and his blood on the field, proclaiming merit for our house; I greatly commend him.’
translations.idiomatic: The Founder said, “Subutai has fought with saddle for pillow and blood on the field, winning honor for our house; I am deeply pleased with him.”

sentences.zh: 賜以大珠、銀罌。

translations.literal: He was granted great pearls and a silver ewer.
translations.idiomatic: He was rewarded with great pearls and a silver ewer.

sentences.zh: 癸未，速不臺上奏，請討欽察。

translations.literal: In guiwei Subutai memorialized, requesting to attack the Qipchaq.
translations.idiomatic: In the guiwei year Subutai memorialized the throne, asking leave to campaign against the Qipchaq.

sentences.zh: 許之。

translations.literal: It was granted.
translations.idiomatic: Permission was granted.

sentences.zh: 遂引兵繞寬定吉思海，展轉至太和嶺，鑿石開道，出其不意。

translations.literal: He then led troops around the Caspian Sea, winding about to Taihe Ridge, hewing stone to open a road, and striking where they did not expect.
translations.idiomatic: He led his army around the Caspian, worked his way to Taihe Ridge, cut a road through the rock, and fell upon the enemy unawares.

sentences.zh: 至則遇其酋長玉裏吉及塔塔哈兒方聚於不租河，縱兵奮擊，其眾潰走。

translations.literal: Upon arrival he encountered their chiefs Yuliji and Tataqar gathered at the Buzu River; he unleashed his troops in fierce attack and their host broke and fled.
translations.idiomatic: When he arrived the Qipchaq chiefs Yuliji and Tataqar were assembled on the Buzu River; he charged hard and their forces scattered in flight.

sentences.zh: 矢及玉裏吉之子，逃於林間，其奴來告而執之，余眾悉降，遂收其境。

translations.literal: An arrow struck Yuliji’s son; he fled into the woods, and his slave came to inform them and he was seized; the rest all submitted, and they thus took their territory.
translations.idiomatic: An arrow struck Yuliji’s son; he fled into the forest, but a slave betrayed his hiding place and he was taken; the rest submitted, and their lands were brought under control.

sentences.zh: 又至阿裏吉河，與斡羅思部大、小密赤思老遇，一戰降之，略阿速部而還。

translations.literal: They again reached the Aliji River, met the Rus’ great and small princes Mstislav, and in one battle subdued them; they raided the Alan tribe and returned.
translations.idiomatic: They pressed on to the Aliji River, met the Rus’ princes great and small—Mstislav—and defeated them in a single battle; they harried the Alan tribe and turned back.

sentences.zh: 欽察之奴來告其主者，速不臺縱為民。

translations.literal: Qipchaq slaves who had come to inform on their masters—Subutai released them as commoners.
translations.idiomatic: Qipchaq slaves who had betrayed their masters to him Subutai set free as ordinary subjects.

sentences.zh: 還，以聞。

translations.literal: Upon return he reported it.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he reported these matters to the throne.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「奴不忠其主，肯忠他人乎？」

translations.literal: The Emperor said, ‘A slave who is not loyal to his master—will he be loyal to others?’
translations.idiomatic: The Founder said, “A slave who betrays his master—how could he be loyal to us?”

sentences.zh: 遂戮之。

translations.literal: He then executed them.
translations.idiomatic: He had them put to death.

sentences.zh: 又奏以滅裏吉、乃蠻、怯烈、杭斤、欽察諸部千戶，通立一軍，從之。

translations.literal: He again memorialized that the centurions of the Merkit, Naiman, Kereit, Hangjin, and Qipchaq tribes be joined into one army, and it was approved.
translations.idiomatic: He further asked that the centurions of the Merkit, Naiman, Kereit, Hangjin, and Qipchaq be formed into a single army under his command, and the request was granted.

sentences.zh: 略也迷裏霍只部，獲馬萬匹以獻。

translations.literal: He raided the Yemili Huozhi tribe, obtained ten thousand horses, and presented them.
translations.idiomatic: He raided the Yemili Huozhi tribe, took ten thousand horses, and presented them to the court.

sentences.zh: 帝欲征河西，以速不臺比年在外，恐父母思之，遣令歸省。

translations.literal: The Emperor wished to campaign in Hexi; because Subutai had been abroad for successive years, fearing his parents might miss him, he sent him to return and visit home.
translations.idiomatic: When the Founder planned a campaign in Hexi, he thought Subutai had been in the field for years and might wish to see his parents, and sent him home on leave.

sentences.zh: 速不臺奏，願從西征。

translations.literal: Subutai memorialized, wishing to follow the western expedition.
translations.idiomatic: Subutai memorialized that he wished to join the western campaign.

sentences.zh: 帝命度大磧以往。

translations.literal: The Emperor ordered him to cross the great desert and proceed.
translations.idiomatic: The Founder ordered him to cross the great desert and advance.

sentences.zh: 丙戌，攻下撒裏畏吾、特勤、赤閔等部，及德順、鎮戎、蘭、會、洮、河諸州，得牝馬五千匹，悉獻於朝。

translations.literal: In bingxu he captured the Sarigu, Teqin, Chimin, and other tribes, and the prefectures Deshun, Zhenrong, Lan, Hui, Tao, and He; he obtained five thousand brood mares and presented them all to court.
translations.idiomatic: In the bingxu year he subdued the Sarigu, Teqin, Chimin, and other tribes, along with the prefectures Deshun, Zhenrong, Lan, Hui, Tao, and He; he took five thousand brood mares and sent them all to the court.

sentences.zh: 丁亥，聞太祖崩，乃還。

translations.literal: In dinghai he heard that the Founder had died and then returned.
translations.idiomatic: In the dinghai year he learned of the Founder’s death and marched home.

sentences.zh: 己丑，太宗即位，以禿滅幹公主妻之。

translations.literal: In jichou Ögedei acceded; he gave him Princess Tümeliken as wife.
translations.idiomatic: In the jichou year, when Ögedei took the throne, he gave Subutai Princess Tümeliken in marriage.

sentences.zh: 從攻潼關，軍失利，帝責之。

translations.literal: He followed in the attack on Tong Pass; the army met defeat and the Emperor reproached him.
translations.idiomatic: He took part in the assault on Tong Pass; the army suffered a setback and the Emperor rebuked him.

sentences.zh: 睿宗時在藩邸，言兵家勝負不常，請令立功自效。

translations.literal: Prince Tolui was then in his princely residence and said that in warfare victory and defeat are not constant, requesting that he be allowed to redeem himself by merit.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Tolui, then in his own establishment, observed that fortune in war is never fixed and asked that Subutai be allowed to redeem himself with fresh deeds.

sentences.zh: 遂命引兵從睿宗經理河南。

translations.literal: He was then ordered to lead troops and follow Tolui in administering Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Subutai was ordered to take his troops and follow Tolui in pacifying Henan.

sentences.zh: 道出牛頭關，遇金將合達帥步騎數十萬待戰。

translations.literal: On the route they passed Niutou Pass and encountered the Jin general Heda leading several hundred thousand infantry and cavalry waiting to give battle.
translations.idiomatic: Marching by way of Niutou Pass, they met the Jin commander Heda at the head of several hundred thousand foot and horse drawn up for battle.

sentences.zh: 睿宗問以方略，速不臺曰：「城居之人不耐勞苦，數挑以勞之，戰乃可勝也。」

translations.literal: Tolui asked his strategy; Subutai said, ‘Town-dwellers cannot endure hardship; repeatedly provoke them to weary them, and then battle can be won.’
translations.idiomatic: Tolui asked his plan of campaign. Subutai replied, “Men who live behind walls cannot bear hardship; harry them again and again until they are worn down, and then you can defeat them in battle.”

sentences.zh: 師集三峰山，金兵圍之數匝。

translations.literal: The army gathered at Sanfeng Mountain; the Jin troops surrounded them in many rings.
translations.idiomatic: The army drew up on Sanfeng Mountain, and the Jin forces closed round them in ring after ring.

sentences.zh: 會風雪大作，其士卒僵仆，師乘之，殺戮殆盡。

translations.literal: It happened that wind and snow rose fiercely; their soldiers stiffened and fell; the army seized the moment and slaughtered nearly all.
translations.idiomatic: A great blizzard struck; the Jin soldiers froze where they stood, and the Mongols fell upon them and cut them down almost to a man.

sentences.zh: 自是金軍不能復振。

translations.literal: From this the Jin army could not recover its strength.
translations.idiomatic: From that day the Jin armies never regained their former strength.

sentences.zh: 壬辰夏，睿宗還駐官山，留速不臺統諸道兵圍汴。

translations.literal: In the summer of renchen Tolui returned to encamp at Guanshan, leaving Subutai to command the armies of all routes in besieging Bian.
translations.idiomatic: In the summer of the renchen year Tolui withdrew to Guanshan, leaving Subutai in command of the combined forces besieging Bianliang.

sentences.zh: 癸巳，金主渡河北走，追敗之於黃龍岡，斬首萬餘級。

translations.literal: In guisi the Jin emperor crossed the Yellow River northward and fled; pursuing, they defeated him at Huanglong Hill and beheaded more than ten thousand.
translations.idiomatic: In the guisi year the Jin emperor fled north across the Yellow River; Subutai overtook him at Huanglong Hill, routed his force, and took more than ten thousand heads.

sentences.zh: 金主復南走歸德府，未幾，復走蔡州。

translations.literal: The Jin emperor again fled south to Guide Prefecture; before long he fled again to Caizhou.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin emperor fled south again to Guide, and soon after pressed on to Caizhou.

sentences.zh: 汴降，俘其后妃及寶器以獻，進圍蔡州。

translations.literal: Bian surrendered; they captured his empresses and consorts and precious vessels and presented them; they advanced to besiege Caizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Bianliang fell; he sent the Jin empresses and the imperial treasure to the court as booty and pressed the siege of Caizhou.

sentences.zh: 甲午，蔡州破，金主自焚死。

translations.literal: In jiawu Caizhou fell; the Jin emperor burned himself to death.
translations.idiomatic: In the jiawu year Caizhou was taken and the Jin emperor died by self-immolation.

sentences.zh: 時汴梁受兵日久，歲饑，人相食，速不臺下令縱其民北渡以就食。

translations.literal: At that time Bianliang had long endured warfare; famine struck the year, and men ate one another; Subutai ordered that the people be allowed to cross north to find food.
translations.idiomatic: Bianliang had been under siege so long that famine set in and people resorted to cannibalism; Subutai ordered that the townspeople be allowed to cross the river northward in search of food.

sentences.zh: 乙未，太宗命諸王拔都西征八赤蠻，且曰：「聞八赤蠻有膽勇，速不臺亦有膽勇，可以勝之。」

translations.literal: In yiwei the Emperor ordered Prince Batu to campaign west against Bachman, saying, ‘I hear Bachman has courage; Subutai also has courage—he can overcome him.’
translations.idiomatic: In the yiwei year Ögedei ordered Prince Batu west against Bachman, adding, “They say Bachman is bold; Subutai is bold too—he can beat him.”

sentences.zh: 遂命為先鋒，與八赤蠻戰。

translations.literal: He was then appointed vanguard and fought Bachman.
translations.idiomatic: Subutai was made vanguard and met Bachman in battle.

sentences.zh: 繼又令統大軍，遂虜八赤蠻妻子於寬田吉思海。

translations.literal: He was again ordered to command the great army and thus captured Bachman’s wife and children by the Caspian Sea.
translations.idiomatic: He was then placed at the head of the main army and took Bachman’s wife and children captive on the shores of the Caspian.

sentences.zh: 八赤蠻聞速不臺至，大懼，逃入海中。

translations.literal: Bachman, hearing Subutai had come, was greatly afraid and fled onto the sea.
translations.idiomatic: When Bachman heard that Subutai was coming he was terrified and fled onto the sea.

sentences.zh: 辛丑，太宗命諸王拔都等討兀魯思部主也烈班，為其所敗，圍禿裏思哥城，不克。

translations.literal: In xinchou the Emperor ordered Princes Batu and others to attack the Rus’ chieftain Yeliban; they were defeated by him and besieged the city of Torzhok but could not take it.
translations.idiomatic: In the xinchou year Ögedei sent Princes Batu and others against the Rus’ prince Yeliban; Yeliban defeated them, and they besieged Torzhok without success.

sentences.zh: 拔都奏遣速不臺督戰，速不臺選哈必赤軍怯憐口等五十人赴之，一戰獲也烈班。

translations.literal: Batu memorialized to send Subutai to supervise the battle; Subutai chose fifty men including Qabichi, Jegünköke, and others to go; in one battle they captured Yeliban.
translations.idiomatic: Batu asked that Subutai be sent to direct the fighting; Subutai picked fifty men, among them Qabichi and Jegünköke, and in a single engagement took Yeliban prisoner.

sentences.zh: 進攻禿裏思哥城，三日克之，盡取兀魯思所部而還。

translations.literal: Advancing to attack Torzhok, they took it in three days, wholly seized the Rus’ domains, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: They assaulted Torzhok and took it in three days, subdued the Rus’ lands, and marched home.

sentences.zh: 經哈咂裏山，攻馬劄兒部主怯憐。

translations.literal: Passing Mount Hazali, they attacked the Magyar chieftain Béla.
translations.idiomatic: Marching by way of Mount Hazali, they attacked King Béla of Hungary.

sentences.zh: 速不臺為先鋒，與諸王拔都、籲裏兀、昔班、哈丹五道分進。

translations.literal: Subutai served as vanguard; with Princes Batu, Orda, Sibian, and Qadan they advanced in five columns.
translations.idiomatic: Subutai led the van while Princes Batu, Orda, Sibian, and Qadan advanced in five separate columns.

sentences.zh: 眾曰：「怯憐軍勢盛，未可輕進。」

translations.literal: The host said, ‘Béla’s army is strong; one must not advance lightly.’
translations.idiomatic: The princes said, “Béla’s army is too strong—we should not press forward rashly.”

sentences.zh: 速不臺出奇計，誘其軍至漷寧河。

translations.literal: Subutai devised a stratagem and lured their army to the Huoning River.
translations.idiomatic: Subutai laid a stratagem and drew the Hungarian army to the Huoning River.

sentences.zh: 諸王軍於上流，水淺，馬可涉，中復有橋。

translations.literal: The princes’ armies were on the upper reach; the water was shallow and horses could ford it; in the middle there was also a bridge.
translations.idiomatic: The princes encamped on the upper reach, where the water was shallow enough for horses to ford and a bridge spanned the stream.

sentences.zh: 下流水深，速不臺欲結筏潛渡，繞出敵後。

translations.literal: Downstream the water was deep; Subutai wished to lash rafts and cross secretly, circling behind the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: Farther down the river ran deep; Subutai meant to raft his men across in secret and take the enemy from the rear.

sentences.zh: 未渡，諸王先涉河與戰。

translations.literal: Before he had crossed, the princes first forded the river and gave battle.
translations.idiomatic: Before he could cross, the princes forded upstream and joined battle.

sentences.zh: 拔都軍爭橋，反為所乘，沒甲士三十人，並亡其麾下將八哈禿。

translations.literal: Batu’s army contended for the bridge and was instead taken advantage of; thirty armored soldiers were drowned, and his subordinate general Baqatu also perished.
translations.idiomatic: Batu’s men fought for the bridge and were worsted; thirty armored warriors were lost, together with his commander Baqatu.

sentences.zh: 既渡，諸王以敵尚眾，欲要速不臺還，徐圖之。

translations.literal: Having crossed, the princes, because the enemy was still numerous, wished to summon Subutai back and plan more slowly.
translations.idiomatic: Once across, the princes, seeing the enemy still strong in number, wanted Subutai to withdraw and deliberate at leisure.

sentences.zh: 速不臺曰：「王欲歸自歸，我不至禿納河馬茶城，不還也。」

translations.literal: Subutai said, ‘If Your Highnesses wish to return, return by yourselves; I shall not turn back until I reach Macha city on the Tuna River.’
translations.idiomatic: Subutai said, “Your Highnesses may go back if you please; I shall not turn back until I reach Macha on the Tuna.”

sentences.zh: 及馳至馬茶城，諸王亦至，遂攻拔之而還。

translations.literal: When he galloped to Macha city the princes also arrived, and they then attacked, captured it, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: He galloped on to Macha; the princes followed, they stormed the town together, and then withdrew.

sentences.zh: 諸王來會，拔都曰：「漷寧河戰時，速不臺救遲，殺我八哈禿。」

translations.literal: When the princes came together, Batu said, ‘At the battle on the Huoning River Subutai’s rescue was late and cost me Baqatu.’
translations.idiomatic: When the princes met, Batu said, “At the Huoning River Subutai was slow to aid us, and my Baqatu was killed.”

sentences.zh: 速不臺曰：「諸王惟知上流水淺，且有橋，遂渡而與戰，不知我於下流結筏未成，今但言我遲，當思其故。」

translations.literal: Subutai said, ‘Your Highnesses only knew the upper water was shallow and that there was a bridge, and so forded and fought; you did not know that downstream I was still lashing rafts and had not finished—now you only say I was late; you should consider the reason.’
translations.idiomatic: Subutai replied, “Your Highnesses saw only the shallow ford and the bridge upstream and rushed to fight; you did not know that downstream my rafts were not yet ready. If you call me slow, consider why.”

sentences.zh: 於是拔都亦悟。

translations.literal: Thereupon Batu also understood.
translations.idiomatic: At that Batu understood.

sentences.zh: 後大會，飲以馬乳及蒲萄酒。

translations.literal: Later at a great assembly they were served kumiss and grape wine.
translations.idiomatic: Later, at a great gathering, they were feasted with kumiss and grape wine.

sentences.zh: 言征怯憐時事，曰：「當時所獲，皆速不臺功也。」

translations.literal: Speaking of the campaign against Béla, they said, ‘What was gained then was all Subutai’s merit.’
translations.idiomatic: Recalling the campaign against Béla, they declared, “Everything we won that day was Subutai’s doing.”

sentences.zh: 壬寅，太宗崩。

translations.literal: In renyin Ögedei died.
translations.idiomatic: In the renyin year Ögedei died.

sentences.zh: 癸卯，諸王大會，拔都欲不往。

translations.literal: In guimao the princes held a great assembly; Batu wished not to go.
translations.idiomatic: In the guimao year the princes were to assemble; Batu did not wish to attend.

sentences.zh: 速不臺曰：「大王於族屬為兄，安得不往？」

translations.literal: Subutai said, ‘Great Prince, among the kin you are the elder brother—how can you not go?’
translations.idiomatic: Subutai said, “Great Prince, you are the eldest among the kin—how can you stay away?”

sentences.zh: 甲辰，遂會於也只裏河。

translations.literal: In jiachen they then met at the Yezhili River.
translations.idiomatic: In the jiachen year they met on the Yezhili River.

sentences.zh: 丙午，定宗即位，既朝會，還家於禿剌河上。

translations.literal: In bingwu Güyük acceded; after the court assembly he returned home on the Tula River.
translations.idiomatic: In the bingwu year, after Güyük’s accession and the court ceremonies, he went home to his estate on the Tula.

sentences.zh: 戊申卒，年七十三。

translations.literal: In wushen he died, aged seventy-three.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the wushen year, at the age of seventy-three.

sentences.zh: 贈效忠宣力佐命功臣、開府儀同三司、上柱國，追封河南王，謚忠定。

translations.literal: He was posthumously granted the title Meritous Minister Who Proclaims Loyalty and Assists the Mandate, Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with the Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon, and Upper Pillar of the State; posthumously enfeoffed as Prince of Henan, with the posthumous name Zhongding.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously honored as Meritous Minister of Loyal Service and Support to the Mandate, Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon, and Upper Pillar of the State; enfeoffed posthumously as Prince of Henan with the temple name Zhongding (“Loyal and Steadfast”).

sentences.zh: 子兀良合臺。

translations.literal: His son was Uriyangqai.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Uriyangqai.

sentences.zh: 兀良合臺

translations.literal: Uriyangqai
translations.idiomatic: Uriyangqai

sentences.zh: 兀良合臺，初事太祖。

translations.literal: Uriyangqai at first served the Founder.
translations.idiomatic: Uriyangqai entered service under the Founder.

sentences.zh: 時憲宗為皇孫，尚幼，以兀良合臺世為功臣家，使護育之。

translations.literal: At that time Möngke was imperial grandson and still young; because Uriyangqai’s family had for generations been a house of meritous ministers, he was made to nurture and protect him.
translations.idiomatic: Möngke was then still a young imperial grandson; because the Uriyangqai family had long been a house of distinguished service, Uriyangqai was charged with his upbringing and protection.

sentences.zh: 憲宗在潛邸，遂分掌宿衛。

translations.literal: When Möngke was in his hidden residence, he then shared command of the palace guard.
translations.idiomatic: When Möngke held his own establishment, Uriyangqai shared command of the palace guard.

sentences.zh: 歲癸巳，領兵從定宗征女真國，破萬奴於遼東。

translations.literal: In the year guisi he led troops following Güyük in campaigning against the Jurchen state and defeated Puxian Wannu in Liaodong.
translations.idiomatic: In the guisi year he led troops with Güyük against the Jurchen realm and defeated Puxian Wannu in Liaodong.

sentences.zh: 繼從諸王拔都征欽察、兀魯思、阿速、孛烈兒諸部。

translations.literal: He then followed Prince Batu in campaigning against the Qipchaq, Rus’, Alan, and Bular tribes.
translations.idiomatic: He then campaigned with Prince Batu against the Qipchaq, Rus’, Alan, and Bular peoples.

sentences.zh: 丙午，又從拔都討孛烈兒乃、捏迷思部，平之。

translations.literal: In bingwu he again followed Batu in attacking the Bular and Mstislav tribes and pacified them.
translations.idiomatic: In the bingwu year he again followed Batu against the Bular and Mstislav peoples and subdued them.

sentences.zh: 己酉，定宗崩。

translations.literal: In jiyou Güyük died.
translations.idiomatic: In the jiyou year Güyük died.

sentences.zh: 拔都與宗室大臣議立憲宗，事久未決。

translations.literal: Batu and the imperial clan ministers deliberated on enthroning Möngke; the matter long went undecided.
translations.idiomatic: Batu and the princes and ministers debated enthroning Möngke, but no decision was reached for a long time.

sentences.zh: 四月，諸王大會，定宗皇后問所宜立，皆惶惑，莫敢對。

translations.literal: In the fourth month the princes held a great assembly; Güyük’s empress asked whom it was fitting to enthrone; all were fearful and confused and dared not reply.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month the princes assembled; Güyük’s empress asked who should succeed, but everyone was afraid and none dared answer.

sentences.zh: 兀良合臺對曰：「此議已先定矣，不可復變。」

translations.literal: Uriyangqai replied, ‘This deliberation was already settled beforehand and cannot be changed again.’
translations.idiomatic: Uriyangqai answered, “That question was settled long ago—it cannot be reopened.”

sentences.zh: 拔都曰：「兀良合臺言是也。」

translations.literal: Batu said, ‘Uriyangqai’s words are correct.’
translations.idiomatic: Batu said, “Uriyangqai is right.”

sentences.zh: 議遂定。

translations.literal: The deliberation was then settled.
translations.idiomatic: The succession was settled.

sentences.zh: 憲宗即位之明年，世祖以皇弟總兵討西南夷烏蠻、白蠻、鬼蠻諸國，以兀良合臺總督軍事。

translations.literal: In the year after Möngke’s accession, Kublai as imperial younger brother commanded troops to attack the southwestern Yi states of Wuman, Baiman, Guiman, and others, with Uriyangqai as overall military commander.
translations.idiomatic: The year after Möngke’s accession, Kublai—as imperial younger brother—took command against the Wuman, Baiman, Guiman, and other southwestern peoples, with Uriyangqai as supreme commander.

sentences.zh: 其鬼蠻，即赤禿哥國也。

translations.literal: The Guiman are the state of Chituoge.
translations.idiomatic: The Guiman were the kingdom of Chituoge.

sentences.zh: 癸丑秋，大軍自旦當嶺入雲南境。

translations.literal: In the autumn of guichou the great army entered Yunnan territory from Dandang Ridge.
translations.idiomatic: In the autumn of the guichou year the main army entered Yunnan by way of Dandang Ridge.

sentences.zh: 摩些二部猷長唆火脫因、塔裹馬來迎降，遂至金沙江。

translations.literal: The chieftains Suohuotuoyin and Taguima of the two Mosuo divisions came to welcome them and submit; they then reached the Jinsha River.
translations.idiomatic: Suohuotuoyin and Taguima, chiefs of the two Mosuo divisions, came out to submit, and the army reached the Jinsha River.

sentences.zh: 兀良合臺分兵入察罕章，蓋白蠻也，所在寨柵，以次攻下之。

translations.literal: Uriyangqai divided his forces to enter Chahanzhang, which is Baiman territory; wherever there were stockades and palisades, they were taken in succession.
translations.idiomatic: Uriyangqai sent detachments into Chahanzhang, Baiman country, and captured stockade after stockade.

sentences.zh: 獨阿塔剌所居半空和寨，依山枕江，牢不可拔。

translations.literal: Only the Bansonghe stockade where Atala dwelt, leaning on the mountain and resting on the river, was firmly impregnable.
translations.idiomatic: Only Atala’s Bansonghe stockade, perched on the mountain above the river, could not be taken.

sentences.zh: 使人覘之，言當先絕其汲道。

translations.literal: He sent men to reconnoiter it; they reported that one should first cut off its water route.
translations.idiomatic: Scouts reported that its water supply should be cut first.

sentences.zh: 兀良合臺率精銳立炮攻之。

translations.literal: Uriyangqai led picked troops, set up artillery, and attacked it.
translations.idiomatic: Uriyangqai led elite troops against it with siege engines.

sentences.zh: 阿塔剌遣人來拒，兀良合臺遣其子阿術迎擊之，寨兵退走。

translations.literal: Atala sent men to resist; Uriyangqai sent his son Aju to meet and strike them, and the stockade soldiers retreated and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Atala sent men to resist; Uriyangqai sent his son Aju to meet them, and the garrison broke and fled.

sentences.zh: 遂並其弟阿叔城俱拔之。

translations.literal: They then together captured his younger brother’s Ashu city as well.
translations.idiomatic: They then took his younger brother’s Ashu city as well.

sentences.zh: 進師取龍首關，翊世祖入大理國城。

translations.literal: Advancing, the army took Longshou Pass and escorted Kublai into the capital of the Dali state.
translations.idiomatic: The army advanced, seized Longshou Pass, and escorted Kublai into the Dali capital.

sentences.zh: 甲寅秋，復分兵取附都善闡，轉攻合剌章水城，屠之。

translations.literal: In the autumn of jiayin they again divided forces to take Fudushanchan, then turned to attack Helazhang Water City and slaughtered it.
translations.idiomatic: In the jiayin autumn they took Fudushanchan, then stormed Helazhang Water City and put it to the sword.

sentences.zh: 合剌章。

translations.literal: Helazhang.
translations.idiomatic: Helazhang.

sentences.zh: 蓋烏蠻也。

translations.literal: It was Wuman territory.
translations.idiomatic: This was Wuman country.

sentences.zh: 前次羅部府，大酋高升集諸部兵拒戰，大破之於洟可浪山下，遂進至烏蠻所都押赤城。

translations.literal: They advanced to Luobu Prefecture; the great chieftain Gao Sheng gathered the troops of all divisions to resist; they were greatly defeated below Tikolang Mountain and then advanced to Yachi city, the Wuman capital.
translations.idiomatic: They moved on Luobu, where the great chief Gao Sheng mustered the tribal levies; Uriyangqai routed them below Tikolang Mountain and pressed on to Yachi, the Wuman capital.

sentences.zh: 城際滇池，三面皆水，既險且堅，選驍勇以炮摧其北門，縱火攻之，皆不克。

translations.literal: The city bordered Dianchi Lake; on three sides there was water; it was both perilous and strong. They chose valiant men to use artillery to smash the north gate and set fire to attack, but all failed.
translations.idiomatic: The city stood on Dianchi, water on three sides, steep and strong; picked warriors battered the north gate with artillery and tried fire assaults, all without success.

sentences.zh: 乃大震鼓鉦，進而作，作而止，使不知所為，如是者七日，伺其困乏，夜五鼓，遣其子阿術潛師躍入，亂斫之，遂大潰。

translations.literal: They then greatly sounded drums and gongs, advancing to strike and ceasing when they struck, so that the enemy did not know what to do; thus for seven days; watching for their exhaustion, at the fifth watch of the night they sent his son Aju with a hidden force to leap in, hack wildly, and the enemy then broke in great rout.
translations.idiomatic: For seven days he kept the drums and gongs thundering—advance, strike, halt—until the defenders were worn down; at the fifth watch he sent Aju with a picked force over the wall in a wild melee, and the garrison collapsed.

sentences.zh: 至昆澤，擒其國王段興智及其渠帥馬合剌昔以獻。

translations.literal: Reaching Kunze, they captured the king Duan Xingzhi and his chieftain Mahelaxi and presented them.
translations.idiomatic: At Kunze they took King Duan Xingzhi and the chieftain Mahelaxi and sent them to court as captives.

sentences.zh: 余眾依阻山谷者，分命裨將也裏、脫伯、押真掩其右，合臺護尉掩其左，約三日卷而內向。

translations.literal: For the remainder who relied on mountain valleys as barriers, he separately ordered lieutenant-generals Yeli, Tuobo, and Yazhen to cover their right, Hetai Huwei their left, agreeing to roll inward within three days.
translations.idiomatic: For those still holding the valleys he sent Yeli, Tuobo, and Yazhen to block the right, Hetai Huwei the left, with orders to close in within three days.

sentences.zh: 及圍合，與阿術引善射者二百騎，期以三日，四面進擊。

translations.literal: When the encirclement closed, with Aju he led two hundred skilled archers on horseback, fixing three days, and attacked from all four sides.
translations.idiomatic: When the ring closed, he and Aju led two hundred mounted archers in a four-sided assault fixed for the third day.

sentences.zh: 兀良合臺陷陣鏖戰，又攻纖寨，拔之。

translations.literal: Uriyangqai plunged into the battle line and fought fiercely; he again attacked Xian stockade and captured it.
translations.idiomatic: Uriyangqai fought in the front rank, then stormed and took Xian stockade.

sentences.zh: 至乾德哥城，兀良合臺病，委軍事於阿術。

translations.literal: Reaching Qiandegge city, Uriyangqai fell ill and entrusted military affairs to Aju.
translations.idiomatic: At Qiandegge Uriyangqai fell ill and turned command over to Aju.

sentences.zh: 環城立炮，以草填塹，眾軍始集，阿術已率所部搏戰城上，城遂破。

translations.literal: They ringed the city with artillery, filled the moat with straw; the main army had only just gathered when Aju already led his division fighting on the wall, and the city was then taken.
translations.idiomatic: They set artillery around the walls and filled the moat with straw; before the main body had fully assembled, Aju was already fighting on the ramparts, and the city fell.

sentences.zh: 乙卯，攻不花合因、阿合阿因等城，阿術先登，取其三城。

translations.literal: In yimao they attacked the cities of Buhuayin, Aheayin, and others; Aju was first to ascend and took the three cities.
translations.idiomatic: In the yimao year they assaulted Buhuayin, Aheayin, and other towns; Aju led the escalade and took all three.

sentences.zh: 又攻赤禿哥山寨，阿術緣嶺而戰，遂拔之。

translations.literal: They again attacked the Chituoge mountain stockade; Aju fought along the ridge and then captured it.
translations.idiomatic: They stormed the Chituoge mountain stronghold; Aju fought along the ridge and took it.

sentences.zh: 乘勝擊破魯魯廝國塔渾城，又取忽蘭城。

translations.literal: Pressing the victory, they smashed the Lulusi state’s Tahun city and again took Hulan city.
translations.idiomatic: Following up, they broke the Lulusi stronghold of Tahun and took Hulan.

sentences.zh: 魯魯廝國大懼，請降。

translations.literal: The Lulusi state was greatly afraid and requested surrender.
translations.idiomatic: The Lulusi kingdom was terrified and sued for peace.

sentences.zh: 阿伯國有兵四萬，不降。

translations.literal: The Abo state had forty thousand troops and would not submit.
translations.idiomatic: The kingdom of Abo had forty thousand men and refused to submit.

sentences.zh: 阿術攻之，入其城，舉國請降。

translations.literal: Aju attacked it, entered its city, and the whole state requested surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Aju attacked, entered the capital, and the whole country surrendered.

sentences.zh: 復攻阿魯山寨，進攻阿魯城，克之。

translations.literal: They again attacked the Alu mountain stockade and advanced to attack Alu city and captured it.
translations.idiomatic: They took the Alu mountain stockade and then the city of Alu.

sentences.zh: 乃搜捕未降者，遇赤禿哥軍於合打臺山，追赴臨崖，盡殺之。

translations.literal: They then searched out and seized those who had not submitted; encountering Chituoge troops at Hedatai Mountain, they pursued them to the cliff edge and killed them all.
translations.idiomatic: Hunting down holdouts, they met Chituoge forces on Hedatai Mountain, drove them to the cliffs, and killed them to the last man.

sentences.zh: 自出師至此，凡二年，平大理五城八府四郡，洎烏、白等蠻三十七部。

translations.literal: From setting out the army until here, in all two years, they pacified Dali’s five cities, eight prefectures, and four districts, reaching thirty-seven divisions of Wuman, Baiman, and others.
translations.idiomatic: In two years from first taking the field they had pacified Dali’s five cities, eight prefectures, and four districts, together with thirty-seven Wuman and Baiman tribes.

sentences.zh: 兵威所加，無不款附。

translations.literal: Wherever military might reached, none failed to submit in sincerity.
translations.idiomatic: Wherever their arms reached, peoples submitted willingly.

sentences.zh: 丙辰，征白蠻國、波麗國，阿術生擒其驍將，獻俘闕下。

translations.literal: In bingchen they campaigned against the Baiman and Poli states; Aju captured alive their fierce generals and presented captives at court.
translations.idiomatic: In the bingchen year they campaigned against Baiman and Poli; Aju took their best generals alive and sent them to the capital as prisoners.

sentences.zh: 詔以便宜取道，與鐵哥帶兒兵合，遂出烏蒙，趨瀘江，刬禿剌蠻三城，卻宋將張都統兵三萬，奪其船二百艘於馬湖江，斬獲不可勝計。

translations.literal: An edict ordered them to take whatever route was expedient and join forces with Tiegedaier’s army; they then issued from Wumeng, hastened to the Lujiang, razed three Tulaman cities, repelled Song General Zhang Dutong’s thirty thousand troops, seized two hundred of their boats on the Mahu River, and beheaded and captured beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: Ordered to take the most direct route and join Tiegedaier, they marched out of Wumeng toward the Lujiang, destroyed three Tulaman towns, routed the Song commander Zhang Dutong’s thirty thousand men, seized two hundred boats on the Mahu River, and killed or captured beyond count.

sentences.zh: 遂通道於嘉定、重慶，抵合州，濟蜀江，與鐵哥帶兒會。

translations.literal: They then opened a route through Jiading and Chongqing, reached Hezhou, crossed the Shu River, and joined Tiegedaier.
translations.idiomatic: They opened a line of advance through Jiading and Chongqing to Hezhou, crossed the Shu River, and linked up with Tiegedaier.

sentences.zh: 丁巳，以雲南平，遣使獻捷於朝，且請依漢故事，以西南夷悉為郡縣，從之。

translations.literal: In dingsi, because Yunnan was pacified, they sent envoys to present victory at court and also requested that, following Han precedent, all southwestern Yi be made into commanderies and districts; it was approved.
translations.idiomatic: In the dingsi year, with Yunnan pacified, they reported victory to court and asked that the southwestern peoples be organized into commanderies and districts on the Han model; the request was granted.

sentences.zh: 賜其軍銀五千兩、彩幣二萬四千匹，授銀印，加大元帥。

translations.literal: His army was granted five thousand taels of silver and twenty-four thousand bolts of colored silks; he was given a silver seal and promoted to grand marshal.
translations.idiomatic: The army was rewarded with five thousand taels of silver and twenty-four thousand bolts of silk; Uriyangqai received a silver seal and the rank of grand marshal.

sentences.zh: 還鎮大理，遂經六盤山至臨洮府，與大營合。

translations.literal: He returned to garrison Dali, then passed by Liupanshan to Lintao Prefecture and joined the main camp.
translations.idiomatic: He returned to garrison Dali, marched by way of Liupanshan to Lintao, and rejoined the main army.

sentences.zh: 月餘，復西征烏蠻。

translations.literal: After more than a month he again campaigned west against the Wuman.
translations.idiomatic: A month later he marched west again against the Wuman.

sentences.zh: 秋九月，遣使招降交趾，不報。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of autumn he sent envoys to summon Jiaozhi to submit; there was no reply.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month he sent envoys to demand the submission of Annam; they made no answer.

sentences.zh: 冬十月，進兵壓境。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of winter he advanced troops pressing on the border.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month he advanced to the frontier.

sentences.zh: 其國主陳日煚，隔江列象騎、步卒甚盛。

translations.literal: Its king Trần Nhật Huệ arrayed elephant cavalry and infantry in great strength across the river.
translations.idiomatic: King Trần Nhật Huệ drew up a strong force of war elephants, cavalry, and infantry on the far bank.

sentences.zh: 兀良合臺分軍為三隊濟江，徹徹都從下流先濟，大帥居中，駙馬懷都與阿術在後。

translations.literal: Uriyangqai divided the army into three columns to cross the river; Chiechie-du crossed first from downstream, the commander-in-chief was in the center, and the imperial son-in-law Huaidu and Aju were in the rear.
translations.idiomatic: Uriyangqai crossed in three columns: Chiechie-du forded downstream first, the commander held the center, and the imperial son-in-law Huaidu and Aju brought up the rear.

sentences.zh: 仍授徹徹都方略曰：「汝軍既濟，勿與之戰，彼必來逆我，駙馬隨斷其後，汝伺便奪其船。

translations.literal: He further instructed Chiechie-du in strategy, saying, ‘Once your army has crossed, do not fight them; they are sure to come against us; the imperial son-in-law will cut off their rear, and you should seize the chance to seize their boats.’
translations.idiomatic: He instructed Chiechie-du: “Once you are across, do not engage; they will come against our center, Huaidu will cut off their retreat, and you are to seize their boats.

sentences.zh: 蠻若潰走，至江無船，必為我擒矣。」

translations.literal: If the barbarians break and flee, reaching the river with no boats, they will surely be captured by us.
translations.idiomatic: If they break and run for the river without boats, we shall take them all.”

sentences.zh: 師既登岸，即縱與戰，徹徹都違命，蠻雖大敗，得駕舟逸去。

translations.literal: Once the army had landed on shore they immediately gave battle; Chiechie-du disobeyed orders; although the barbarians were greatly defeated, they were able to take boats and escape.
translations.idiomatic: As soon as the troops landed they joined battle; Chiechie-du disobeyed orders, and though the Annamese were routed, they escaped by boat.

sentences.zh: 兀良合臺怒曰：「先鋒違我節度，軍有常刑。」

translations.literal: Uriyangqai angrily said, ‘The vanguard disobeyed my command; the army has fixed punishments.’
translations.idiomatic: Uriyangqai said in anger, “The vanguard defied my orders—the army has its penalties.”

sentences.zh: 徹徹都懼，飲藥死。

translations.literal: Chiechie-du, in fear, drank poison and died.
translations.idiomatic: Chiechie-du, in fear, took poison and died.

sentences.zh: 兀良合臺入交趾，為久駐計，軍令嚴肅，秋毫無犯。

translations.literal: Uriyangqai entered Jiaozhi, planning a long stay; military discipline was strict and not the slightest thing was violated.
translations.idiomatic: Uriyangqai entered Annam intending a long occupation; discipline was strict and the troops did not harm so much as a blade of grass.

sentences.zh: 越七日，日煚請內附，於是置酒大饗軍士。

translations.literal: After seven days Trần Nhật Huệ requested to submit inwardly; thereupon they set out wine and feasted the soldiers greatly.
translations.idiomatic: Within seven days Trần Nhật Huệ asked to submit, and Uriyangqai gave a great feast for the army.

sentences.zh: 還軍柙赤城。

translations.literal: The army returned to Xiachi city.
translations.idiomatic: The army withdrew to Xiachi.

sentences.zh: 戊午，引兵入宋境，其地炎瘴，軍士皆病，遇敵少卻，亡軍士四人。

translations.literal: In wuwu he led troops into Song territory; the land was hot and malarial, and the soldiers all fell ill; meeting the enemy they retreated slightly, losing four soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: In the wuwu year he led troops into Song territory; the climate was feverish and malarial, the men sickened, a skirmish cost four lives, and the column drew back.

sentences.zh: 阿術還戰，擒其卒十二人，其援復至，阿術以三十騎，阿馬禿繼以五十騎擊走之。

translations.literal: Aju returned to fight, captured twelve of their soldiers; their reinforcements came again; Aju with thirty horsemen, and Amadu following with fifty horsemen, struck and drove them off.
translations.idiomatic: Aju turned back, took twelve prisoners, and when reinforcements arrived he with thirty horse and Amadu with fifty drove them off.

sentences.zh: 時兀良合臺亦病，將旋師，阿術戰馬五十匹夜為禿剌蠻所掠，入告兀良合臺曰：「吾馬盡為盜掠去，將何以行？」

translations.literal: At that time Uriyangqai was also ill and about to withdraw the army; fifty of Aju’s war horses were plundered at night by the Tulaman; he entered and reported to Uriyangqai, saying, ‘My horses have all been stolen by bandits—how am I to march?’
translations.idiomatic: Uriyangqai too was ill and preparing to withdraw when Tulaman raiders stole fifty of Aju’s horses by night; Aju told him, “Our horses are gone—how can we march?”

sentences.zh: 即分軍搜訪，知有三寨藏馬山顛。

translations.literal: He immediately divided the army to search; they learned that three stockades on the mountain summit were hiding horses.
translations.idiomatic: Troops were sent to search and found three stockades hoarding horses on the mountaintop.

sentences.zh: 阿術親率將士攀崖而上，破其諸寨，生擒賊酋，盡得前後所盜馬千七百匹，乃屠柙赤城。

translations.literal: Aju personally led officers and soldiers climbing the cliff upward, broke their stockades, captured the bandit chieftain alive, wholly recovered the seventeen hundred horses stolen before and after, and then slaughtered Xiachi city.
translations.idiomatic: Aju led his men up the cliffs, stormed the stockades, took the bandit chief alive, recovered all seventeen hundred stolen horses, and put Xiachi to the sword.

sentences.zh: 憲宗遣使諭旨，約明年正月會軍長沙，乃率四王騎兵三千，蠻、僰萬人，破橫山寨，辟老蒼關，徇宋內地。

translations.literal: Möngke sent envoys with instructions, fixing the first month of the next year to assemble the army at Changsha; he then led three thousand cavalry of the four princes and ten thousand Yi and Bo troops, captured Hengshan stockade, opened Laochang Pass, and swept through Song interior territory.
translations.idiomatic: Möngke ordered a rendezvous at Changsha in the first month of the coming year; Uriyangqai took three thousand horse of the four princes and ten thousand tribal auxiliaries, took Hengshan stockade, forced Laochang Pass, and raided deep into Song territory.

sentences.zh: 宋陳兵六萬以俟。

translations.literal: The Song arrayed sixty thousand troops to await them.
translations.idiomatic: The Song drew up sixty thousand men to meet him.

sentences.zh: 遣阿術與四王潛自間道沖其中堅，大敗之，盡殺其眾。

translations.literal: He sent Aju and the four princes secretly by a bypath to charge their center; they were greatly defeated and their host wholly slaughtered.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Aju and the four princes by a hidden path into the enemy center, routed them, and slaughtered the whole force.

sentences.zh: 乘勝擊逐，蹴貴州，蹂象州，入靜江府，連破辰、沅二州，直抵潭州城下。

translations.literal: Pressing the victory in pursuit, they trampled Guizhou, ravaged Xiangzhou, entered Jingjiang Prefecture, successively broke Chen and Yuan prefectures, and went straight to below Tanzhou city.
translations.idiomatic: Following up, they overran Guizhou, ravaged Xiangzhou, entered Jingjiang, took Chen and Yuan prefectures, and marched to the walls of Tanzhou.

sentences.zh: 潭州出兵二十萬，斷我歸路。

translations.literal: Tanzhou sent out two hundred thousand troops to cut off their line of retreat.
translations.idiomatic: Tanzhou sent two hundred thousand men to cut off their retreat.

sentences.zh: 兀良合臺遣阿術與大納、玉龍帖木兒軍其前，而自與四王軍其後，夾擊破之。

translations.literal: Uriyangqai sent Aju with Dana and Yulong Temür to face their front, while he himself with the four princes faced their rear, and in a pincer attack defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: Uriyangqai sent Aju, Dana, and Yulong Temür against their front while he and the four princes struck from the rear and broke them between two fires.

sentences.zh: 兵自入敵境，轉鬥千里，未嘗敗北。

translations.literal: From entering enemy territory the army fought turning battles for a thousand li and never once suffered defeat.
translations.idiomatic: From the border to Tanzhou they fought for a thousand li without a single defeat.

sentences.zh: 大小十三戰，殺宋兵四十餘萬，擒其將大小三人。

translations.literal: In great and small engagements numbering thirteen battles, they killed more than four hundred thousand Song troops and captured three of their generals, great and small.
translations.idiomatic: In thirteen engagements they killed more than four hundred thousand Song soldiers and took three generals prisoner.

sentences.zh: 其州又遣兵來攻，追至門濠，掩溺殆盡，乃不敢復出。

translations.literal: The prefecture again sent troops to attack; pursuing them to the moat before the gate, they drowned nearly all and then dared not come out again.
translations.idiomatic: When the city sent another sortie, they chased the Song troops to the moat and drowned most of them; the garrison did not dare sally again.

sentences.zh: 壁城下月餘。

translations.literal: They encamped below the city walls for more than a month.
translations.idiomatic: They invested the city for more than a month.

sentences.zh: 時世祖已渡江駐鄂州，遣也裏蒙古領兵二千人來援，且加勞問。

translations.literal: At that time Kublai had already crossed the Yangzi and was stationed at Ezhou; he sent Yeli Mongolu leading two thousand troops to reinforce them and also sent words of consolation and inquiry.
translations.idiomatic: Kublai had crossed the Yangzi and was at Ezhou; he sent Yeli Mongolu with two thousand men as reinforcements and a message of praise.

sentences.zh: 遂自鄂州之滸黃洲北渡，與大軍合。

translations.literal: They then from Ezhou’s Huhuang Isle crossed northward and joined the great army.
translations.idiomatic: They crossed north from Huhuang Isle near Ezhou and rejoined the main army.

sentences.zh: 庚申，世祖即位。

translations.literal: In gengshen Kublai acceded.
translations.idiomatic: In the gengshen year Kublai took the throne.

sentences.zh: 夏四月，兀良合臺至上都。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of summer Uriyangqai reached Shangdu.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of summer Uriyangqai arrived at Shangdu.

sentences.zh: 後十二年卒，年七十二。

translations.literal: Twelve years later he died, aged seventy-two.
translations.idiomatic: Twelve years later he died, at the age of seventy-two.

sentences.zh: 子阿術，自有傳。

translations.literal: His son Aju has his own biography.
translations.idiomatic: His son Aju has a separate biography.

sentences.zh: ○按竺邇

translations.literal: Anzhu'er
translations.idiomatic: Anzhu'er

sentences.zh: 按竺邇，雍古氏。

translations.literal: Anzhu'er was of the Yonggu tribe.
translations.idiomatic: Anzhu'er was a Yonggu tribesman.

sentences.zh: 其先居雲中塞上，父<黑旦>公，為金群牧使。

translations.literal: His ancestors dwelt on the Yunzhong frontier; his father Duke Heidan served the Jin as commissioner of herd pastures.
translations.idiomatic: His forebears lived on the Yunzhong frontier; his father, Duke Heidan, was Jin commissioner of herd pastures.

sentences.zh: 歲辛未，驅所牧馬來歸太祖，終其官。

translations.literal: In the year xinwei he drove the horses he pastured to come and submit to the Founder, and died in office.
translations.idiomatic: In the xinwei year he drove his herds to the Founder and submitted; he died in that office.

sentences.zh: 按竺邇幼鞠於外祖術要甲家，訛言為趙家，因姓趙氏。

translations.literal: Anzhu'er in youth was reared at his maternal grandfather Shuyao Jia’s home; by corrupted speech he was called of the Zhao family, and therefore took the surname Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: Raised in his maternal grandfather Shuyao Jia’s household, he was known in local speech as one of the Zhao clan and took the surname Zhao.

sentences.zh: 年十四，隸皇子察合臺部。

translations.literal: At age fourteen he was attached to Prince Chagatai’s division.
translations.idiomatic: At fourteen he entered the service of Prince Chagatai.

sentences.zh: 嘗從大獵，射獲數麋，有二虎突出，射之皆死。

translations.literal: He once followed a great hunt, shot and obtained several elk; two tigers burst forth and he shot them both dead.
translations.idiomatic: On a great hunt he brought down several elk; when two tigers charged out he killed them both with his bow.

sentences.zh: 由是以善射名，皇子深器愛之。

translations.literal: From this he gained fame for skilled archery, and the prince deeply valued and loved him.
translations.idiomatic: He won renown as an archer, and the prince held him in high favor.

sentences.zh: 甲戌，太祖西征尋思幹、阿裏麻裏等國，以功為千戶。

translations.literal: In jiaxu the Founder campaigned west against the states of Xingsigan, Alimali, and others; for merit he was made a centurion.
translations.idiomatic: In the jiaxu year, on the western campaign against Xingsigan, Alimali, and other states, he was made a centurion for his service.

sentences.zh: 丁亥，從征積石州，先登，拔其城。

translations.literal: In dinghai he followed the campaign against Jishi Prefecture, was first to ascend, and captured its city.
translations.idiomatic: In the dinghai year he joined the assault on Jishi, was first over the wall, and took the city.

sentences.zh: 圍河州，斬首四十級。

translations.literal: Besieging Hezhou, he beheaded forty heads.
translations.idiomatic: At the siege of Hezhou he took forty heads.

sentences.zh: 破臨洮，攻德順，斬首百餘級。

translations.literal: He broke Lintao, attacked Deshun, and beheaded more than a hundred heads.
translations.idiomatic: He stormed Lintao, attacked Deshun, and took more than a hundred heads.

sentences.zh: 攻鞏昌，駐兵秦州。

translations.literal: He attacked Gongchang and stationed troops at Qinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He attacked Gongchang and encamped at Qinzhou.

sentences.zh: 太宗即位，尊察合臺為皇兄，以按竺邇為元帥。

translations.literal: When Ögedei acceded, he honored Chagatai as imperial elder brother and made Anzhu'er marshal.
translations.idiomatic: When Ögedei took the throne he honored Chagatai as imperial elder brother and made Anzhu'er marshal.

sentences.zh: 戊子，鎮刪丹州，自燉煌置驛抵玉關，通西域，從定關隴。

translations.literal: In wuzi he garrisoned Shandan Prefecture; from Dunhuang he established post stations reaching Yumen Pass, opening the Western Regions, and followed in pacifying the Guanlong region.
translations.idiomatic: In the wuzi year he garrisoned Shandan, set up post stations from Dunhuang to Yumen Pass to open the Western Regions, and helped pacify Guanlong.

sentences.zh: 辛卯，從圍鳳翔，按竺邇分兵攻西南隅，城上礌石亂下，選死士先登，拔其城，斬金將劉興哥。

translations.literal: In xinmao he followed the siege of Fengxiang; Anzhu'er divided troops to attack the southwest corner; catapult stones rained chaotically from the wall; he chose death-defying warriors to ascend first, captured the city, and beheaded the Jin general Liu Xingge.
translations.idiomatic: In the xinmao year, at the siege of Fengxiang, he attacked the southwest corner; despite a hail of stones from the walls his picked men were first up, the city fell, and the Jin general Liu Xingge was beheaded.

sentences.zh: 分兵攻西和州，宋將強俊領眾數萬，堅壁清野，以老我師。

translations.literal: Dividing forces to attack Xihe Prefecture, the Song general Qiang Jun led several tens of thousands, fortified walls and cleared the countryside, to wear out our army.
translations.idiomatic: He detached troops against Xihe, where the Song general Qiang Jun with tens of thousands fortified the walls, stripped the countryside, and tried to wear the Mongols down.

sentences.zh: 按竺邇率死士罵城下，挑戰。

translations.literal: Anzhu'er led death-defying warriors to curse below the city and challenge battle.
translations.idiomatic: Anzhu'er led picked men to the foot of the walls and taunted the garrison into battle.

sentences.zh: 俊怒，悉眾出陣，按竺邇佯走，俊追之，因以奇兵奪其城。

translations.literal: Jun in anger sent out his entire host to array; Anzhu'er feigned flight; Jun pursued him, and thereby with surprise troops seized their city.
translations.idiomatic: Qiang Jun in fury marched out with his whole force; Anzhu'er feigned retreat, and when Jun pursued, a hidden detachment seized the city.

sentences.zh: 伏兵要其歸，轉戰數十里，斬首數千級，擒俊。

translations.literal: Ambush troops intercepted their return; fighting turned for several tens of li; they beheaded several thousand heads and captured Jun.
translations.idiomatic: Ambushers cut off their retreat; after fighting for miles they took several thousand heads and captured Qiang Jun.

sentences.zh: 余眾退保仇池，進擊拔之，從拔平涼，慶陽、邠、原、寧皆降。

translations.literal: The remainder retreated to hold Qiu Pool; advancing they attacked and captured it; following they took Pingliang; Qingyang, Bin, Yuan, and Ning all submitted.
translations.idiomatic: The survivors fell back on Qiu Pool; he stormed it, took Pingliang, and Qingyang, Bin, Yuan, and Ning all submitted.

sentences.zh: 涇州復叛，殺守將郭元恕，眾議屠之，按竺邇但誅首惡。

translations.literal: Jingzhou rebelled again, killing the garrison commander Guo Yuanxu; the assembly debated slaughtering it, but Anzhu'er only executed the chief evildoers.
translations.idiomatic: Jingzhou rebelled again and killed the commander Guo Yuanxu; when others urged a massacre, Anzhu'er punished only the ringleaders.

sentences.zh: 師還原州，降民棄老幼，夜亡走。

translations.literal: The army returned to Yuanzhou; the submitted people abandoned the old and young and fled by night.
translations.idiomatic: When the army withdrew to Yuanzhou, the submitted populace abandoned their elders and children and fled by night.

sentences.zh: 眾曰：「此必反也，宜誅之以警其餘。」

translations.literal: The assembly said, "They will surely rebel again; they ought to be executed to warn the rest."
translations.idiomatic: The officers said, "They are bound to rebel—execute them as a warning to the others."

sentences.zh: 按竺邇曰：「此輩懼吾驅之北徙耳。」

translations.literal: Anzhu'er said, "These people only fear that we will drive them north to migrate."
translations.idiomatic: Anzhu'er replied, "They are only afraid we mean to drive them north in resettlement."

sentences.zh: 遣人諭之曰：「汝等若走，以軍法治罪，父母妻子並誅矣。

translations.literal: He sent men to instruct them, saying, "If you flee, you will be punished under military law—parents, wives, and children all executed.
translations.idiomatic: He sent messengers to tell them, "If you run, military law will condemn you—and your parents, wives, and children with you.

sentences.zh: 汝歸，保無他。

translations.literal: Return, and I guarantee no further harm.
translations.idiomatic: Come back, and I pledge you will come to no harm.

sentences.zh: 明年草青，具牛酒迎師於此州。」

translations.literal: Next year when the grass turns green, prepare cattle and wine to welcome the army in this prefecture."
translations.idiomatic: Next spring, when the grass greens, bring cattle and wine to welcome the army here."

sentences.zh: 民皆復歸。

translations.literal: The people all returned.
translations.idiomatic: The people all came back.

sentences.zh: 豪民陳茍集數千人潛新寨諸洞，眾議以火攻之。

translations.literal: The powerful man Chen Gou gathered several thousand men hiding in the caves around Xincai; the assembly debated attacking with fire.
translations.idiomatic: A local magnate, Chen Gou, mustered several thousand men and hid in the cave strongholds of Xincai; the officers urged a fire attack.

sentences.zh: 按竺邇曰：「招諭不出，攻之未晚。」

translations.literal: Anzhu'er said, "Summon and persuade them; if they will not come out, attacking will not be too late."
translations.idiomatic: Anzhu'er said, "Try summons and persuasion first; if they refuse to come out, we can still attack."

sentences.zh: 遂偕數騎抵寨，縱馬解弓矢，召茍遙語，折矢與為誓。

translations.literal: He then took several horsemen to the stockade, loosened bow and arrows while riding freely, called Gou from afar to speak, broke an arrow, and swore an oath with him.
translations.idiomatic: He rode to the stockade with only a few companions, let his horse roam and laid aside bow and arrows, called Gou from a distance, broke an arrow, and pledged faith with him.

sentences.zh: 茍即相呼羅拜，謝更生之恩，皆降。

translations.literal: Gou at once called out and bowed in prostration, thanked him for sparing their lives, and all submitted.
translations.idiomatic: Gou and his men cried out and prostrated themselves, thanking him for their lives, and all surrendered.

sentences.zh: 金人守潼關，攻之，戰於扇車回，不克。

translations.literal: The Jin held Tong Pass; they attacked, fought at Shanche Hui, and could not take it.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin garrison held Tong Pass; the Mongols assaulted it and fought at Shanche Hui but failed to break through.

sentences.zh: 睿宗分兵由山南入金境，按竺邇為先鋒，趣散關。

translations.literal: Tolui divided his forces to enter Jin territory south of the mountains; Anzhu'er served as vanguard, hurrying toward San Pass.
translations.idiomatic: Tolui sent a column south of the Qinling into Jin territory; Anzhu'er led the vanguard toward San Pass.

sentences.zh: 宋人已燒絕棧道，復由兩當縣出魚關，軍沔州。

translations.literal: The Song had burned and severed the plank road; they again went out through Liangdang County via Yu Pass and encamped at Mianzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The Song had burned the plank roads; the army turned through Liangdang County and Yu Pass instead and marched on Mianzhou.

sentences.zh: 宋制置使桂如淵守興元。

translations.literal: Song Pacification Commissioner Gui Ruyuan held Xingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: The Song pacification commissioner Gui Ruyuan held Xingyuan.

sentences.zh: 按竺邇假道於如淵曰：「宋讎金久矣，何不從我兵鋒，一洗國恥。

translations.literal: Anzhu'er asked passage of Ruyuan, saying, "Song has long hated Jin—why not follow the point of our army's spears and wash away the nation's shame at once?
translations.idiomatic: Anzhu'er asked Ruyuan for passage, saying, "Song has nursed hatred of Jin for generations—why not march with our spearhead and wipe out that disgrace in one stroke?

sentences.zh: 今欲假道南鄭，由金、洋達唐、鄧，會大兵以滅金，豈獨為吾之利？

translations.literal: Now we wish to borrow the road through Nanzheng, reach Tang and Deng via Jin and Yang, join the great army to destroy Jin—is that benefit ours alone?
translations.idiomatic: We mean to pass through Nanzheng, reach Tang and Deng by way of Jin and Yang, and join the main force to destroy Jin—is that advantage ours alone?

sentences.zh: 亦宋之利也。」

translations.literal: It is Song's benefit as well."
translations.idiomatic: It would serve Song's interest too."

sentences.zh: 如淵度我軍壓境，勢不徒還，遂遣人導我師由武休關東抵鄧州，西破小關。

translations.literal: Ruyuan reckoned our army pressed the border and would not return empty-handed; he therefore sent men to guide our forces east through Wuxiu Pass to Dengzhou, and west to break Little Pass.
translations.idiomatic: Ruyuan judged that with our army on his border we would not withdraw without gain; he sent guides to lead our troops east through Wuxiu Pass to Dengzhou and west to storm Little Pass.

sentences.zh: 金人大駭，謂我軍自天而下。

translations.literal: The Jin were greatly terrified, saying our army had descended from heaven.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin were appalled, saying our army had fallen from the sky.

sentences.zh: 其平章完顏合達、樞密使移剌蒲阿帥十七都尉，兵數十萬，相拒於鄧。

translations.literal: Their Grand Councillor Wanyan Heda and Censor-in-Chief Yelü Pu'a led seventeen commanders-in-chief with an army of several hundred thousand, opposing at Deng.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Councillor Wanyan Heda and Censor-in-Chief Yelü Pu'a commanded seventeen divisional generals and several hundred thousand men to block them at Deng.

sentences.zh: 我師不與戰，直趣鈞州，與親王按赤臺等兵合，陳三峰山下。

translations.literal: Our army did not engage in battle, but went straight to Junzhou, joined with Imperial Prince Anchitai and others' forces, and arrayed below Mount Sanfeng.
translations.idiomatic: Our forces refused battle, marched straight on Junzhou, joined Imperial Prince Anchitai's troops, and formed up below Mount Sanfeng.

sentences.zh: 會天大雪，金兵成列。

translations.literal: It happened that heaven sent great snow; the Jin army formed ranks.
translations.idiomatic: Heavy snow fell; the Jin army stood in battle order.

sentences.zh: 按竺邇先率所部精兵迎擊於前，諸軍乘之，金師敗績。

translations.literal: Anzhu'er first led his elite troops to meet the attack in front; the other armies followed up, and the Jin army was utterly defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Anzhu'er led his picked troops in the first shock; the rest of the army pressed the advantage, and the Jin force was routed.

sentences.zh: 癸巳，金主奔蔡。

translations.literal: On guisi, the Jin emperor fled to Cai.
translations.idiomatic: On the guisi day the Jin emperor fled to Cai.

sentences.zh: 十二月，從圍蔡。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, he followed in the siege of Cai.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month he took part in the siege of Cai.

sentences.zh: 甲午，金亡。

translations.literal: On jiawu, Jin perished.
translations.idiomatic: On the jiawu day Jin fell.

sentences.zh: 初，金將郭斌自鳳翔突圍出，保金、蘭、定、會四州。

translations.literal: Earlier, the Jin general Guo Bin broke out from Fengxiang and held the four prefectures of Jin, Lan, Ding, and Hui.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier the Jin general Guo Bin had broken out of Fengxiang and held Jin, Lan, Ding, and Hui prefectures.

sentences.zh: 至是命按竺邇往取之，圍斌於會州。

translations.literal: At this time he was ordered to send Anzhu'er to take them; he besieged Bin at Huizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Anzhu'er was now dispatched to reduce them and besieged Bin at Huizhou.

sentences.zh: 食盡將走，敗之於城門。

translations.literal: When provisions were exhausted and Bin was about to flee, he defeated him at the city gate.
translations.idiomatic: When supplies ran out and Bin tried to break out, Anzhu'er defeated him at the gate.

sentences.zh: 兵入城巷戰，死傷甚眾。

translations.literal: Troops entered the city and fought in the lanes; dead and wounded were very many.
translations.idiomatic: The troops entered and fought street by street; casualties on both sides were heavy.

sentences.zh: 斌手劍驅其妻子聚一室，焚之。

translations.literal: Bin with sword in hand drove his wife and children into one room and burned them.
translations.idiomatic: Sword in hand, Bin drove his wife and children into one room and set it afire.

sentences.zh: 已而自投火中。

translations.literal: Then he himself threw himself into the fire.
translations.idiomatic: Then he threw himself into the flames.

sentences.zh: 有女奴自火中抱兒出，泣授人曰：「將軍盡忠，忍使絕嗣，此其兒也，幸哀而收之。」

translations.literal: A serving woman emerged from the fire holding a child, weeping as she handed him to someone, saying, "The general gave his utmost loyalty; how can we bear to cut off his line? This is his child—please pity him and take him in."
translations.idiomatic: A maidservant ran from the fire carrying a boy and, weeping, gave him to a bystander: "The general died loyal to the end—do not let his line end. This is his son; have mercy and keep him."

sentences.zh: 言畢，復赴火死。

translations.literal: When she had finished speaking, she again entered the fire and died.
translations.idiomatic: With that she returned to the fire and perished.

sentences.zh: 按竺邇聞之惻然，命保其孤。

translations.literal: Anzhu'er, hearing this, was deeply moved and ordered the orphan preserved.
translations.idiomatic: Anzhu'er was moved and ordered the child kept safe.

sentences.zh: 遂定四州。

translations.literal: He thus secured the four prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: The four prefectures were then pacified.

sentences.zh: 金將汪世顯守鞏州，皇子闊端圍之，未下。

translations.literal: The Jin general Wang Shixian held Gongzhou; Prince Kuoduan besieged it but had not taken it.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin general Wang Shixian held Gongzhou; Prince Kuoduan besieged the city but could not reduce it.

sentences.zh: 遣按竺邇等往招之，世顯率眾來降。

translations.literal: He sent Anzhu'er and others to summon him; Shixian led his host to submit.
translations.idiomatic: Anzhu'er was sent to negotiate; Shixian led his troops out in surrender.

sentences.zh: 皇兄嘉其材勇，賞賚甚厚，賜名拔都，拜征行大元帥。

translations.literal: The imperial elder brother praised his talent and courage, rewarded him richly, bestowed the name Batu, and appointed him campaign grand marshal.
translations.idiomatic: An imperial prince commended his skill and valor, lavished rewards on him, gave him the name Batu, and made him campaign grand marshal.

sentences.zh: 丙申，大軍伐蜀，皇子出大散關，分兵令宗王穆直等出陰平郡，期會於成都。

translations.literal: On bingshen, the great army invaded Shu; the prince marched out via Great San Pass, divided forces ordering Prince Muzhi and others out via Yinping commandery, to rendezvous at Chengdu.
translations.idiomatic: On the bingshen day the main army invaded Shu; a prince marched through Great San Pass while Prince Muzhi and others were sent through Yinping commandery, all to converge on Chengdu.

sentences.zh: 按竺邇領炮手兵為先鋒，破宕昌，殘階州。

translations.literal: Anzhu'er led catapult troops as vanguard, captured Dangchang, and ravaged Jiezhou.
translations.idiomatic: Anzhu'er led the artillerymen as vanguard, took Dangchang, and laid waste to Jiezhou.

sentences.zh: 攻文州，守將劉祿，數月不下，諜知城中無井，乃奪其汲道，率勇士梯城先登，殺守陴者數十人，遂拔其城，祿死之。

translations.literal: Attacking Wenzhou, the garrison commander Liu Lu held out for months; spies learned the city had no wells, so they seized the water route, led brave men up ladders to scale the wall first, killed several dozen defenders on the ramparts, then captured the city; Lu died.
translations.idiomatic: At Wenzhou the defender Liu Lu held out for months until scouts reported the city had no wells; Anzhu'er cut off the water supply, led picked men up scaling ladders to the wall, killed dozens on the battlements, and took the city; Liu Lu was killed.

sentences.zh: 因招徠吐蕃酋長勘拖孟迦等十族，皆賜以銀符。

translations.literal: Thereupon he recruited Tibetan chieftains including Kuntuo Mengjia of ten clans, all bestowed silver tally tokens.
translations.idiomatic: He then won over ten Tibetan clans led by chieftain Kuntuo Mengjia, granting each a silver tally.

sentences.zh: 略定龍州。

translations.literal: He broadly secured Longzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Longzhou was brought under control.

sentences.zh: 遂與大散軍合，進克成都。

translations.literal: He then joined the Great San army and advanced to capture Chengdu.
translations.idiomatic: He joined the column from Great San Pass and marched to take Chengdu.

sentences.zh: 師還，而成都復叛。

translations.literal: The army returned, but Chengdu rebelled again.
translations.idiomatic: The army withdrew, but Chengdu rose again.

sentences.zh: 丁酉，按竺邇言於宗王曰：「隴州縣方平，人心猶貳，西漢陽當隴蜀之沖，宋及吐蕃利於入寇，宜得良將以鎮之。」

translations.literal: On dingyou, Anzhu'er said to the prince, "Longzhou's counties have just been pacified but hearts are still divided; West Hanyang lies on the throat between Long and Shu—Song and Tibet can easily raid; a good general should be stationed there."
translations.idiomatic: On the dingyou day Anzhu'er told the prince, "Longzhou has only just been settled and loyalties are still uncertain; West Hanyang sits on the road between Long and Shu, where Song and Tibet can raid at will—a capable commander should hold it."

sentences.zh: 宗王曰：「安反側，制寇賊，此上策也，然無以易汝。」

translations.literal: The prince said, "To settle the wavering and check raiders—that is the best policy, yet there is no one to replace you."
translations.idiomatic: The prince replied, "To quiet the restless and hold off raiders is the right course—but there is no one to replace you."

sentences.zh: 遂分蒙古千戶五人，隸麾下以往。

translations.literal: He therefore assigned five Mongol chiliarchs under his command to go there.
translations.idiomatic: Five Mongol chiliarchs were placed under his command and sent with him.

sentences.zh: 按竺邇命侯和尚南戍沔州之石門，術魯西戍階州之兩水，謹斥堠，嚴巡邏，西南諸州不敢犯之。

translations.literal: Anzhu'er ordered Hou Heshang to garrison south at Shimen in Mianzhou, and Shulusi to garrison west at Liangshui in Jiezhou; with careful scouts and strict patrols, the southwestern prefectures dared not violate the border.
translations.idiomatic: Anzhu'er posted Hou Heshang at Shimen in southern Mianzhou and Shulusi at Liangshui in western Jiezhou; with tight scouting and patrols, none of the southwestern prefectures dared cross the line.

sentences.zh: 戊戌，從元帥塔海率諸翼兵伐蜀，克隆慶。

translations.literal: On wuxu, following Marshal Taqai he led allied wing troops to invade Shu and captured Longqing.
translations.idiomatic: On the wuxu day, under Marshal Taqai, he led the allied wings into Shu and took Longqing.

sentences.zh: 己亥，攻重慶。

translations.literal: On jihai, they attacked Chongqing.
translations.idiomatic: On the jihai day they assaulted Chongqing.

sentences.zh: 庚子，圖萬州。

translations.literal: On gengzi, they invested Wanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On the gengzi day they besieged Wanzhou.

sentences.zh: 宋人將舟師數百艘逆流迎戰。

translations.literal: The Song deployed several hundred warships upstream to meet battle.
translations.idiomatic: The Song sent several hundred warships upstream to meet them.

sentences.zh: 按竺邇順流率勁兵，乘巨筏，浮革舟於其間，弓弩兩射，宋人不能敵，敗諸夔門。

translations.literal: Anzhu'er downstream led crack troops aboard great rafts with leather boats floated among them; bowmen and crossbowmen shot from both sides; the Song could not resist and were defeated at Kuimen.
translations.idiomatic: Anzhu'er moved downstream with picked troops on great rafts, leather boats lashed among them; archers and crossbowmen fired from both banks until the Song could not stand and were broken at Kuimen.

sentences.zh: 辛丑，伐西川，破二十餘城。

translations.literal: On xinchou, they invaded West Chuan and captured more than twenty cities.
translations.idiomatic: On the xinchou day they overran western Sichuan and took more than twenty cities.

sentences.zh: 成都守將田顯開北門以納師。

translations.literal: Chengdu's garrison commander Tian Xian opened the north gate to admit the army.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Xian, the Chengdu garrison commander, opened the north gate to let the army in.

sentences.zh: 宋制置使陳隆之出奔，追獲之，縛至漢州，令誘降守將王夔。

translations.literal: Song Pacification Commissioner Chen Longzhi fled; they pursued and captured him, bound him to Hanzhou, and ordered him to persuade garrison commander Wang Kui to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: The Song pacification commissioner Chen Longzhi fled; he was caught, bound, and brought to Hanzhou to persuade the defender Wang Kui to surrender.

sentences.zh: 夔不降，進兵攻之。

translations.literal: Kui would not submit; they advanced to attack him.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Kui refused; the army marched to attack him.

sentences.zh: 夔夜驅火牛，突圍出奔，遂斬隆之。

translations.literal: Kui by night drove fire-oxen, broke out and fled; they then beheaded Longzhi.
translations.idiomatic: Kui sent fire-oxen against the lines by night and broke out; Longzhi was beheaded.

sentences.zh: 壬寅，會大軍破遂寧、瀘、敘等州。

translations.literal: On renyin, joining the great army they captured Suining, Lu, Xu, and other prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: On the renyin day the main force took Suining, Lu, Xu, and other prefectures.

sentences.zh: 癸卯，破資州。

translations.literal: On guimao, they captured Zizhou.
translations.idiomatic: On the guimao day Zizhou fell.

sentences.zh: 庚戌，按竺邇安輯涇、邠二州。

translations.literal: On gengxu, Anzhu'er pacified and settled Jing and Bin prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: On the gengxu day Anzhu'er pacified Jing and Bin prefectures.

sentences.zh: 宋制置使余玠攻興元，文州降將王德新乘隙自階州叛，執扈、牛二鎮將，領眾千餘走江油。

translations.literal: Song Pacification Commissioner Yu Jie attacked Xingyuan; Wang Dexin, a surrendered general of Wenzhou, seized an opening to rebel from Jiezhou, seized the two garrison commanders Hu and Niu, and led more than a thousand men to flee toward Jiangyou.
translations.idiomatic: When the Song pacification commissioner Yu Jie attacked Xingyuan, Wang Dexin—a former Wenzhou defector—seized the moment to rebel from Jiezhou, captured the garrison commanders Hu and Niu, and fled toward Jiangyou with more than a thousand men.

sentences.zh: 憲宗召按竺邇還舊鎮。

translations.literal: Möngke summoned Anzhu'er back to his former post.
translations.idiomatic: Möngke recalled Anzhu'er to his old command.

sentences.zh: 按竺邇遣將直搗江油，奪扈、牛以歸。

translations.literal: Anzhu'er sent a general straight to strike Jiangyou and recovered Hu and Niu.
translations.idiomatic: Anzhu'er sent a commander straight at Jiangyou and brought Hu and Niu back.

sentences.zh: 中統元年，世祖即位，親王有異謀者，其將阿藍答兒、渾都海圖據關隴。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhongtong, when Kublai took the throne, among the imperial princes were those with divergent designs; their generals Arigadai and Qunduqai seized and held Guan and Long.
