translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Zhongtong, when Kublai ascended the throne, some imperial princes harbored rival designs, and their generals Arigadai and Qunduqai seized Guan and Long.

sentences.zh: 時按竺邇以老，委軍於其子。

translations.literal: At the time Anzhu'er, being old, entrusted his army to his son.
translations.idiomatic: Anzhu'er was then elderly and entrusted his command to his son.

sentences.zh: 帝遣宗王哈丹、哈必赤、阿曷馬西討。

translations.literal: The Emperor dispatched the imperial princes Hadan, Qabichi, and Ahema to campaign in the west.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor sent the imperial princes Hadan, Qabichi, and Ahema west to suppress them.

sentences.zh: 按竺邇曰：「今內難方殷，浸亂關隴，豈臣子安臥之時耶？吾雖老，尚能破賊。」

translations.literal: Anzhu'er said: "Now internal trouble is pressing and disorder is spreading through Guan and Long—how can this be a time for a subject to rest at ease? Though I am old, I can still break the rebels."
translations.idiomatic: Anzhu'er said, "Internal crisis is pressing and disorder is spreading through Guan and Long—how can a subject rest at ease? Though I am old, I can still break the rebels."

sentences.zh: 遂引兵出刪丹之耀碑谷，從阿曷馬，與之合戰。

translations.literal: He then led troops out through Yaobei Valley in Shandan and, following Ahema, joined battle with him.
translations.idiomatic: He then led troops out through Yaobei Valley in Shandan, followed Ahema, and joined the fight.

sentences.zh: 會大風，晝晦，戰至晡，大敗之，斬馘無算。

translations.literal: A great wind arose, daylight grew dark, and battle continued until the afternoon watch; he inflicted a great defeat and cut off heads beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: A great wind arose and daylight turned murky; the fighting lasted until afternoon, when he won a crushing victory and cut down the enemy beyond count.

sentences.zh: 按竺邇與總帥汪良臣獲阿藍答兒、渾都海等。

translations.literal: Anzhu'er, together with supreme commander Wang Liangchen, captured Arigadai, Qunduqai, and others.
translations.idiomatic: Anzhu'er and supreme commander Wang Liangchen captured Arigadai, Qunduqai, and others.

sentences.zh: 捷聞，帝錫璽書襃美，賜弓矢錦衣。

translations.literal: When news of victory arrived, the Emperor bestowed an imperial-seal letter of praise and granted bow, arrows, and brocade robes.
translations.idiomatic: When victory was reported, the Emperor sent an imperial-seal letter of praise and granted bows, arrows, and brocade robes.

sentences.zh: 四年，卒，年六十九。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he died, aged sixty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he died, aged sixty-nine.

sentences.zh: 延祐元年，贈推忠佐運功臣、太保、儀同三司、上柱國，封秦國公，諡武宣。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yanyou he was posthumously enfeoffed as Meritorious Minister Who Supports Loyalty and Aids the Dynasty, Grand Guardian, Grand General of State with Ceremonial Honors Equal to the Three Excellencies, and Senior Pillar of State; enfeoffed as Duke of Qin; posthumous name Wuxuan.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Yanyou he was posthumously enfeoffed as Meritorious Minister of Supporting Loyalty and Aiding the Dynasty, Grand Guardian, Grand General of State with the Ceremonial Standing of the Three Excellencies, and Senior Pillar of State; created Duke of Qin, with the posthumous name Wuxuan.

sentences.zh: 子十人，徹理、國寶最知名。

translations.literal: He had ten sons; Cherig and Guobao were the most renowned.
translations.idiomatic: He had ten sons; Cherig and Guobao were the best known.

sentences.zh: 徹理襲職為元帥。

translations.literal: Cherig inherited the post as marshal.
translations.idiomatic: Cherig inherited the marshal's commission.

sentences.zh: 丁巳，從父攻瀘州，降宋將劉整。

translations.literal: On dingsi, following his father he attacked Luzhou and got Song general Liu Zheng to submit.
translations.idiomatic: On the dingsi day he followed his father against Luzhou and won the surrender of the Song general Liu Zheng.

sentences.zh: 宋將姚德壁雲頂山，戊午，大軍圍之。

translations.literal: Song general Yao De fortified on Cloud-Peak Mountain; on wuwu the great army besieged it.
translations.idiomatic: The Song general Yao De held Cloud-Peak Mountain; on the wuwu day the main army encircled him.

sentences.zh: 徹理率部兵由水門先登，破其壁，德降。

translations.literal: Cherig led his troops through the water gate to ascend first, broke his fortifications, and De submitted.
translations.idiomatic: Cherig led his men through the water gate to the top, broke the fort, and Yao De surrendered.

sentences.zh: 後以病廢，卒。

translations.literal: Later he was disabled by illness and died.
translations.idiomatic: He was later incapacitated by illness and died.

sentences.zh: 國寶一名黑梓，少擊劍學書，倜儻好義，有謀略。

translations.literal: Guobao, also named Heizi, in youth practiced swordsmanship and studied writing; he was free-spirited, fond of righteousness, and possessed of stratagem.
translations.idiomatic: Guobao, also called Heizi, trained in swordplay and letters as a youth; he was bold, upright, and shrewd.

sentences.zh: 父為元帥，軍務悉以委之，故所至多捷。

translations.literal: When his father was marshal, he entrusted all military affairs to him; hence wherever he went victories were many.
translations.idiomatic: While his father held the marshal's post he entrusted all military affairs to him, and wherever Guobao went victory followed.

sentences.zh: 從攻重慶，降宋都統張實，並掠合州以歸。

translations.literal: Following the attack on Chongqing, he got Song commander-in-chief Zhang Shi to submit and also plundered Hezhou on the return.
translations.idiomatic: In the assault on Chongqing he won over the Song commander Zhang Shi and on the return carried off Hezhou.

sentences.zh: 中統元年，從攻阿藍答兒有功。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhongtong, following the attack on Aranash he performed merit.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of the Zhongtong era he distinguished himself in the campaign against Aranash.

sentences.zh: 阿藍答兒叛將火都據吐蕃之點西嶺。

translations.literal: Aranash's rebel general Huodu held Xidian Ridge in Tibet.
translations.idiomatic: Huodu, a rebel of Aranash, held Xidian Ridge in Tibetan country.

sentences.zh: 國寶攝帥事，討之。

translations.literal: Guobao acted as commander and marched to suppress him.
translations.idiomatic: Guobao took command in his stead and marched against him.

sentences.zh: 眾欲速戰，國寶曰：「此窮寇也，宜少緩，以計破之。」

translations.literal: The host wished quick battle; Guobao said, "These are cornered bandits; we should delay slightly and destroy them by stratagem."
translations.idiomatic: The men wanted a quick fight; Guobao said, "These are desperate fugitives—hold back a little and break them by strategy."

sentences.zh: 遂以精兵襲其後。

translations.literal: He then sent elite troops to strike their rear.
translations.idiomatic: He sent picked troops to strike from the rear.

sentences.zh: 火都欲西走，國寶據險要之，挑戰則斂兵自固。

translations.literal: Huodu wished to flee west; Guobao held the passes to block him; when challenged he drew in his troops and held firm.
translations.idiomatic: Huodu tried to break west; Guobao seized the defiles and blocked him, and when provoked he pulled his men in and stood fast.

sentences.zh: 相持兩月，潛兵出其不意，擒殺之。

translations.literal: After two months of stalemate, hidden troops struck unexpectedly and captured and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: After two months of standoff, a hidden detachment took him by surprise and killed him.

sentences.zh: 捷聞，賜弓矢、金綺。

translations.literal: When news of victory arrived, he was granted bow and arrows and gold brocade.
translations.idiomatic: When victory was reported, he received bows, arrows, and gold brocade.

sentences.zh: 初，按竺邇之告老，制命徹理襲征行元帥。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Anzhu'er petitioned to retire, an imperial order had Cherig inherit the campaign marshalcy.
translations.idiomatic: When Anzhu'er had petitioned to retire, the throne ordered Cherig to inherit the campaign marshal's post.

sentences.zh: 徹理以病不視事，國寶乃謂諸弟曰：「昔我先人，耀兵西陲，大功既集，關隴雖寧，而西戎未靖，此吾輩立功之秋也。」

translations.literal: Cherig through illness did not attend to affairs; Guobao then said to his brothers, "In old days our forebear displayed the army on the western frontier; great merit was gathered, and though Guan and Long were settled, the western Rong were not pacified—this is our season to win merit."
translations.idiomatic: Cherig, ill, could not govern; Guobao told his brothers, "Our forebear once carried the army in glory on the western marches; though Guan and Long were quieted, the western tribes were not yet settled—this is our time to earn distinction."

sentences.zh: 乃遣謝鼎與弟國能，持金帛說降吐蕃，酋長勘陀孟迦從國寶入覲。

translations.literal: He then sent Xie Ding and his brother Guoneng, bearing gold and silks to persuade Tibetans to submit; chieftain Kuntuo Mengjia followed Guobao to audience.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Xie Ding and his brother Guoneng with gold and silks to win over the Tibetans; the chieftain Kuntuo Mengjia came to court with Guobao.

sentences.zh: 國寶奏曰：「文州山川險厄，控庸蜀，拒吐蕃，宜城文州，屯兵鎮之。」

translations.literal: Guobao memorialized, "Wenzhou's mountains and rivers are perilous; it controls Yong and Shu and blocks Tibet—it is fitting to wall Wenzhou and station troops to garrison it."
translations.idiomatic: Guobao memorialized, "Wenzhou's terrain is rugged; it commands the roads to Yong and Shu and holds Tibet at bay—Wenzhou should be walled and garrisoned."

sentences.zh: 從之，授國寶三品印，為蒙古漢軍元帥，兼文州吐蕃萬戶府達魯花赤，與勘陀孟迦皆賜金符。

translations.literal: It was approved; Guobao was granted a third-rank seal, made Mongol and Han army marshal, concurrently darughachi of the Wenzhou Tibetan wanhu prefecture; both he and Kuntuo Mengjia were granted gold tally tokens.
translations.idiomatic: The court agreed; Guobao received a third-rank seal, was made marshal of Mongol and Han forces and darughachi of the Wenzhou Tibetan wanhu office, and both he and Kuntuo Mengjia were given gold tallies.

sentences.zh: 時扶州諸羌未附，國寶宣上威德，於是呵哩禪波哩揭諸酋長皆歸款，從國寶入覲。

translations.literal: At that time the Qiang of Fuzhou had not yet submitted; Guobao proclaimed the court's majesty and virtue; thereupon chieftains including Helizhen Bolijie all offered allegiance and followed Guobao to audience.
translations.idiomatic: The Qiang of Fuzhou had not yet submitted; Guobao proclaimed the throne's power and grace, and chieftains including Helizhen Bolijie all came over and followed him to court.

sentences.zh: 國寶圖山川形勢以獻，詔授呵哩禪波哩揭為萬戶，賜金虎符，諸酋長為千戶，皆賜金符。

translations.literal: Guobao mapped the terrain and presented it; an edict appointed Helizhen Bolijie as wanhu, granted a gold tiger tally; the chieftains were made chiliarchs, all granted gold tally tokens.
translations.idiomatic: Guobao mapped the country and presented the charts; Helizhen Bolijie was made wanhu and given a gold tiger tally, and the chieftains were made chiliarchs, each granted a gold tally.

sentences.zh: 賜國寶金幣。

translations.literal: Guobao was granted gold coins.
translations.idiomatic: Guobao was rewarded with gold.

sentences.zh: 國寶治文州有善政。

translations.literal: Guobao governed Wenzhou with good policies.
translations.idiomatic: Guobao governed Wenzhou well.

sentences.zh: 至元四年卒。

translations.literal: He died in the fourth year of Zhiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the fourth year of the Zhiyuan era.

sentences.zh: 延祐元年，贈推誠佐理功臣、光祿大夫、平章政事、柱國，封梁國公，謚忠定。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yanyou, posthumously granted Faithful Assistant Merit Criterion, Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, Grand Councillor, Pillar of State; enfeoffed as Duke of Liang; posthumous name Zhongding.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of the Yanyou era he was posthumously made Faithful Assistant Merit Criterion, Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, Grand Councillor, and Pillar of State, enfeoffed Duke of Liang, with the posthumous name Loyal and Steadfast.

sentences.zh: 子世榮、世延。

translations.literal: Sons Shirong and Shiyan.
translations.idiomatic: His sons were Shirong and Shiyan.

sentences.zh: 初，國寶將卒，以世榮幼，命弟國安襲其職。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Guobao was about to die, because Shirong was young he ordered his brother Guo'an to inherit the post.
translations.idiomatic: As Guobao lay dying, Shirong being still young, he had his brother Guo'an succeed to the post.

sentences.zh: 國安既襲蒙古漢軍元帥，兼文州吐蕃萬戶府達魯花赤，後以其兄國寶安邊功，賜金虎符，進昭勇大將軍。

translations.literal: Guo'an having inherited Mongol and Han army marshal and concurrent darughachi of Wenzhou Tibetan wanhu prefecture, later for his elder brother Guobao's merit in pacifying the frontier he was granted a gold tiger tally and promoted to General of Manifest Courage.
translations.idiomatic: Guo'an took over as marshal of Mongol and Han forces and darughachi of the Wenzhou Tibetan wanhu office; later, for his brother Guobao's frontier service, he received a gold tiger tally and was promoted to General of Manifest Courage.

sentences.zh: 十五年，討叛王吐魯於六盤，獲之，請解職授世榮。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year, suppressing rebel prince Tulu at Liupan, he captured him and requested to resign and transfer the post to Shirong.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year he captured the rebel prince Tulu at Liupan and asked to step down in favor of Shirong.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「人爭而汝讓，可以敦薄俗。」

translations.literal: The emperor said, "When others contend and you yield, that can enrich shallow custom."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "When others scramble for office and you yield, you may set right a mean age."

sentences.zh: 錄其六盤功，進昭毅大將軍、招討使。

translations.literal: His merit at Liupan was recorded; he was promoted to General of Manifest Resolution and pacification commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: His service at Liupan was entered in the record and he was promoted to General of Manifest Resolution and made pacification commissioner.

sentences.zh: 世榮，襲懷遠大將軍、蒙古漢軍元帥，兼文州吐蕃萬戶府達魯花赤。

translations.literal: Shirong inherited General Who Cherishes the Distant, marshal of Mongol and Han armies, and concurrently served as darughachi of the Wenzhou Tibetan wanhu prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Shirong succeeded to the post of General Who Cherishes the Distant and marshal of Mongol and Han forces, with the concurrent office of darughachi of the Wenzhou Tibetan wanhu command.

sentences.zh: 後以功進安遠大將軍、吐蕃宣慰使議事都元帥，佩三珠虎符。

translations.literal: Later for merit he was promoted to General Who Pacifies the Distant, chief commander for deliberation as pacification commissioner of Tibet, and wore a three-pearl tiger tally.
translations.idiomatic: Later, for his service, he was promoted to General Who Pacifies the Distant and chief commander of the Tibetan pacification commission, and was granted a three-pearl tiger tally.

sentences.zh: 世延，中書平章政事。

translations.literal: Shiyan, grand councillor of the Central Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Shiyan served as grand councillor of the Central Secretariat.

sentences.zh: ○畏答兒

translations.literal: Weida'er
translations.idiomatic: Weida'er

sentences.zh: 畏答兒，忙兀人。

translations.literal: Weida'er was a Mangwu tribesman.
translations.idiomatic: Weida'er was of the Mangwu tribe.

sentences.zh: 其先剌真八都兒，有二子，次名忙兀兒，始別為忙兀氏。

translations.literal: His ancestor was Chazhen Badu'er, who had two sons; the younger was named Mangwu'er, and from him the Mangwu clan first separated.
translations.idiomatic: His forebear Chazhen Badu'er had two sons; the younger, Mangwu'er, founded the separate Mangwu line.

sentences.zh: 畏答兒其六世孫也。

translations.literal: Weida'er was his sixth-generation descendant.
translations.idiomatic: Weida'er was six generations removed from him.

sentences.zh: 與兄畏翼俱事太祖。

translations.literal: He and his elder brother Weiyi both served the Founder.
translations.idiomatic: He and his elder brother Weiyi both entered the Founder's service.

sentences.zh: 時大疇強盛，畏翼率其屬歸之，畏答兒力止之，不聽，追之，又不肯還，畏答兒乃還事太祖。

translations.literal: At that time Tachou was powerful; Weiyi led his followers to submit to him. Weida'er strenuously stopped him, but he would not listen; Weida'er pursued him, yet he still refused to return, and Weida'er thereupon returned to serve the Founder.
translations.idiomatic: Tachou was then at the height of his power. Weiyi took their men over to him; Weida'er tried hard to stop him, was ignored, followed after him, and was rebuffed again—then returned alone to the Founder.

sentences.zh: 太祖曰：「汝兄既去，汝獨留此何為？」

translations.literal: The Founder said, "Your elder brother having gone, what are you alone remaining here for?"
translations.idiomatic: The Founder asked, "Your brother has gone—why do you stay here alone?"

sentences.zh: 畏答兒無以自明，取矢折而誓曰：「所不終事主者，有如此矢。」

translations.literal: Weida'er had no way to prove himself; he took an arrow, broke it, and swore, "If I do not serve my lord to the end, let it be as this arrow."
translations.idiomatic: Unable to answer, Weida'er broke an arrow and swore, "May I perish like this shaft if I fail to serve my lord to the end."

sentences.zh: 太祖察其誠，更名為薛禪，約為按達。

translations.literal: The Founder perceived his sincerity, renamed him Setsen, and pledged him as anda.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing his good faith, the Founder renamed him Setsen and took him as blood-brother.

sentences.zh: 薛禪者，聰明之謂也；

translations.literal: Setsen means "clever."
translations.idiomatic: Setsen means "wise."

sentences.zh: 按達者，定交不易之謂也。

translations.literal: Anda means "a fixed bond not easily changed."
translations.idiomatic: Anda means a sworn bond that is not lightly broken.

sentences.zh: 太祖與克烈王罕對陳於哈剌真，師少不敵。

translations.literal: The Founder and the Kerait king Wang Han faced each other in battle array at Harjan; his army was few and could not match the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: At Harjan the Founder drew up against Wang Han of the Kerait, but his force was too small to hold the field.

sentences.zh: 帝命兀魯一軍先發，其將術徹臺橫鞭馬鬛不應。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered the Uriangqai army to advance first; its general Shichi Tai laid his whip across the horse's mane and would not respond.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered the Uriangqai to lead the attack; their commander Shichi Tai lay his whip across his mount's mane and hung back.

sentences.zh: 畏答兒奮然曰：「我猶鑿也，諸君斧也，鑿匪斧不入，我請先入，諸軍繼之，萬一不還，有三黃頭兒在，唯上念之。」

translations.literal: Weida'er said with ardor, "I am like a chisel and you all are axes; a chisel cannot enter without an axe—I ask to go in first, with the armies following. If I should not return, I have three yellow-headed sons; may the sovereign remember them."
translations.idiomatic: Weida'er cried out, "I am the chisel and you the axe—the chisel cannot bite wood alone. Let me lead; the rest follow. If I fall, I leave three young sons—may my lord not forget them."

sentences.zh: 遂先出陷陣，大敗之，至晡時，猶追逐不已，敕使止之，乃還。

translations.literal: He then went out first and broke into the enemy formation, routing them utterly; even by late afternoon he still pursued without cease, until an order came to stop him, and only then did he return.
translations.idiomatic: He charged first, broke the enemy line, and drove them in rout; he was still chasing at dusk when an order recalled him.

sentences.zh: 腦中流矢，創甚，帝親傅以善藥，留處帳中，月餘卒，帝深惜之。

translations.literal: An arrow struck his brain; the wound was grave. The emperor personally applied good medicine, kept him in the tent, and after more than a month he died; the emperor deeply regretted it.
translations.idiomatic: An arrow had pierced his head; the wound was mortal. The emperor tended him himself and kept him in camp, but within a month he died, to the Founder's deep grief.

sentences.zh: 及王罕滅，帝以其將只裏吉實抗畏答兒，乃分只裏吉民百戶隸其子，且使世世歲賜不絕。

translations.literal: When Wang Han was destroyed, because his general Jilig had actually resisted Weida'er, the emperor assigned a hundred households of Jilig's people to his son, and ordered that generation after generation the annual grants never cease.
translations.idiomatic: After Wang Han's fall, because his general Jilig had fought Weida'er, the emperor assigned a hundred households of Jilig's people to Weida'er's son and decreed that the yearly stipend should continue for all his line.

sentences.zh: 仍令收完忙兀人民之散亡者。

translations.literal: He was also ordered to gather back the Mangwu people who had been scattered and lost.
translations.idiomatic: He was also charged with reclaiming Mangwu tribesmen who had been scattered.

sentences.zh: 太宗思其功，復以北方萬戶封其子忙哥為郡王。

translations.literal: Ögedei, mindful of his merit, again enfeoffed his son Mangge as a commandery prince with a northern wanhu.
translations.idiomatic: Mindful of Weida'er's service, Ögedei made his son Mangge a commandery prince with ten thousand northern households.

sentences.zh: 歲丙申，忽都忽大料漢民，分城邑以封功臣，授忙哥泰安州民萬戶。

translations.literal: In the bingchen year, Huduqu took a great census of Han people and divided cities and towns to enfeoff meritorious ministers; Mangge was granted ten thousand households of the people of Taian prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the bingchen year Huduqu registered the Han population for feudal grants; Mangge received ten thousand Taian households.

sentences.zh: 帝訝其少，忽都忽對曰：「臣今差次，惟視舊數多寡，忙哥舊才八百戶。」

translations.literal: The emperor was surprised at how small it was; Huduqu replied, "In assigning ranks today, I look only at the old counts, more or less; Mangge's old register was only eight hundred households."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor thought the grant too small. Huduqu answered, "I allot by the old registers alone—Mangge had only eight hundred households."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「不然，畏答兒封戶雖少，戰功則多，其增封為二萬戶，與十功臣同。

translations.literal: The emperor said, "That will not do. Weida'er's enfeoffed households were few, but his battle merit was great—increase his grant to twenty thousand households, the same as the Ten Meritorious Ministers.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "No. Weida'er's fief was small, but his battlefield deeds were great—raise it to twenty thousand households, equal to the Ten Meritorious Ministers.

sentences.zh: 為諸侯者，封戶皆異其籍。」

translations.literal: For the feudatories, enfeoffed households were all taken from separate registers."
translations.idiomatic: Each prince's grant was drawn from distinct registers."

sentences.zh: 兀魯爭曰：「忙哥舊兵不及臣之半，今封顧多於臣。」

translations.literal: Uriangqai protested, "Mangge's old force was not half of mine, yet his grant now exceeds mine."
translations.idiomatic: Uriangqai objected, "Mangge's old contingent was less than half mine—why does his grant now surpass mine?"

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「汝忘而先橫鞭馬鬛時耶？」

translations.literal: The emperor said, "Have you forgotten when you first laid your whip across the horse's mane?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Have you forgotten laying your whip across your horse's mane?"

sentences.zh: 兀魯遂不敢言。

translations.literal: Uriangqai then dared say no more.
translations.idiomatic: Uriangqai fell silent.

sentences.zh: 忙哥卒，孫只里瓦䚟、乞答䚟，曾孫忽都忽、兀乃忽里、哈赤，俱襲封為郡王。

translations.literal: Mangge died; his grandsons Jiliwaqar and Qidaqar, and his great-grandsons Huduqu, Unaihuli, and Kachi, all inherited the enfeoffment as commandery princes.
translations.idiomatic: After Mangge's death, his grandsons Jiliwaqar and Qidaqar and his great-grandsons Huduqu, Unaihuli, and Kachi each succeeded to the commandery princedom.

sentences.zh: ○博羅歡伯都

translations.literal: Boluohuan; Bedu
translations.idiomatic: Boluohuan; Bedu

sentences.zh: 博羅歡，畏答兒幼子蘸木曷之孫，瑣魯火都之子也。

translations.literal: Boluohuan was the son of Suoluhuodu, grandson of Zhamuhe, youngest son of Weida'er.
translations.idiomatic: Boluohuan was the son of Suoluhuodu and grandson of Zhamuhe, Weida'er's youngest son.

sentences.zh: 時諸侯王及十功臣各有斷事官，博羅歡年十六，為本部斷事官。

translations.literal: At that time each feudal prince and each of the Ten Meritorious Ministers had a judge of cases; Boluohuan at age sixteen became judge of cases for his own division.
translations.idiomatic: Each prince and each of the Ten Meritorious Ministers then had his own judge of cases; at sixteen Boluohuan became judge for his own branch.

sentences.zh: 從世祖討阿裏不哥，數有功，帝喜而賜馬四十匹，金幣稱之。

translations.literal: He followed Kublai in campaigning against Ariq Böke and repeatedly achieved merit; the emperor was pleased and bestowed forty horses and gold commensurate with his deeds.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Kublai against Ariq Böke and won repeated distinction; the emperor rewarded him with forty horses and gold in proportion to his service.

sentences.zh: 中統三年，李亶叛。

translations.literal: In the third year of Zhongtong, Li Tan rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of the Zhongtong era Li Tan rebelled.

sentences.zh: 命帥忙兀一軍圍濟南，分兵掠益都、萊州，悉平之。

translations.literal: He was ordered to command a Mangwu army to besiege Jinan, divide troops to raid Yidu and Laizhou, and pacify them all.
translations.idiomatic: He was ordered to lead a Mangwu force against Jinan, sent columns to overrun Yidu and Laizhou, and reduced them all.

sentences.zh: 詔錄燕南獄，讞決明允，賜衣一襲。

translations.literal: An edict ordered him to review prisons south of the Yan region; his judgments were clear and fair, and he was granted one suit of clothing.
translations.idiomatic: He was ordered to review the prisons of Yan South; his verdicts were lucid and just, and he was given a suit of robes.

sentences.zh: 皇子雲南王忽哥赤為其省臣寶合丁毒死，事覺，中書擇可治其獄者四人，奏上，皆不稱旨。

translations.literal: Prince Hugochi, Prince of Yunnan, had been poisoned to death by his provincial minister Baoheding; when the matter came to light, the Central Secretariat chose four men capable of handling the case and submitted them, but none pleased the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Hugochi of Yunnan had been poisoned by his provincial minister Baoheding; when the crime was exposed, the Central Secretariat nominated four men to try the case, but none satisfied the throne.

sentences.zh: 丞相線真以博羅歡聞，帝可其奏。

translations.literal: Grand Councillor Xianzhen memorialized recommending Boluohuan; the emperor approved the memorial.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Councillor Xianzhen recommended Boluohuan, and the emperor assented.

sentences.zh: 博羅歡辭曰：「臣不敢愛死，第年少不知書，恐誤事耳。」

translations.literal: Boluohuan declined, saying, "Your servant does not shrink from death, but being young and unlearned, I fear I may mishandle the affair."
translations.idiomatic: Boluohuan declined, saying, "I do not fear death, but I am young and barely literate—I may botch the case."

sentences.zh: 帝乃以吏部尚書別帖木兒輔其行。

translations.literal: The emperor then sent Minister of Personnel Bietiemuer to assist him on the journey.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then sent the Minister of Personnel Bietiemuer to assist him.

sentences.zh: 未至雲南，寶合丁密以金六籯迎饋，祈勿究其事。

translations.literal: Before he reached Yunnan, Baoheding secretly sent six chests of gold to welcome and bribe him, begging that the matter not be pursued.
translations.idiomatic: Before he reached Yunnan, Baoheding secretly sent six chests of gold as a bribe, pleading that the case go no further.

sentences.zh: 博羅歡慮其握兵僥外，拒之恐致變，陽諾曰：「吾橐不能容，可且持歸，待我取之。」

translations.literal: Boluohuan, fearing that Baoheding held troops and relied on distance from the capital, thought refusal might provoke rebellion; he feigned assent, saying, "My purse cannot hold it—take it back for now, and I shall collect it later."
translations.idiomatic: Boluohuan feared that Baoheding, holding troops in a distant province, might rebel if rebuffed; he pretended to agree, saying, "My purse is too small—keep it for now until I come for it."

sentences.zh: 博羅歡至，則竟其獄，誅毒王者，而歸其金於省。

translations.literal: When Boluohuan arrived, he brought the case to completion, executed the man who had poisoned the prince, and returned the gold to the provincial office.
translations.idiomatic: When Boluohuan arrived he saw the case through, executed the prince's poisoner, and turned the gold over to the provincial administration.

sentences.zh: 陛見，帝顧謂線真曰：「卿舉得其人矣。」

translations.literal: At audience before the throne, the emperor turned and said to Xianzhen, "Your recommendation found the right man."
translations.idiomatic: At audience the emperor turned to Xianzhen and said, "You chose well."

sentences.zh: 賜黃金五十兩，詔忙兀事無大小，悉統於博羅歡。

translations.literal: He was granted fifty taels of gold, and an edict ordered that all Mangwu affairs, great and small, be placed under Boluohuan's overall command.
translations.idiomatic: He was given fifty taels of gold, and an edict placed all Mangwu affairs, great and small, under his command.

sentences.zh: 授昭勇大將軍、右衛親軍都指揮使，大都則專右衛，上都則兼三衛。

translations.literal: He was appointed General of Manifest Courage and commander-in-chief of the Right Guard Household Army; at Dadu he commanded only the Right Guard, at Shangdu he commanded all three guards jointly.
translations.idiomatic: He was made General of Manifest Courage and commander of the Right Guard Household Army—sole commander of the Right Guard at Dadu, and of all three guards at Shangdu.

sentences.zh: 會伐宋，授金吾衛上將軍、中書右丞。

translations.literal: When a campaign against Song was launched, he was appointed General-in-Chief of the Golden Guard and Right Vice-Chancellor of the Central Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: When war with Song began, he was made General-in-Chief of the Golden Guard and Right Vice-Chancellor of the Central Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 詔分大軍為二，右軍受伯顏、阿術節度，左軍受博羅歡節度。

translations.literal: An edict divided the great army in two: the right wing was placed under the command of Bayan and Aju, the left wing under Boluohuan.
translations.idiomatic: The main force was split in two—the right wing under Bayan and Aju, the left under Boluohuan.

sentences.zh: 俄兼淮東都元帥，罷山東經略司，而以其軍悉隸焉。

translations.literal: Soon he was also made overall commander of Huaidong; the Shandong pacification commission was abolished, and its troops were all placed under him.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made overall commander of Huaidong as well; the Shandong pacification office was abolished and its troops assigned to him.

sentences.zh: 遂軍於下邳，召將佐謀曰：「清河城小而固，與昭信、淮安、泗州為掎角，猝未易拔。

translations.literal: He then encamped at Xiapi, summoned his officers, and said, "Qinghe city is small but strong; with Zhaoxin, Huai'an, and Sizhou it forms a pincer, and cannot quickly be taken.
translations.idiomatic: He encamped at Xiapi and called his commanders together. "Qinghe is small but stout," he said, "and with Zhaoxin, Huai'an, and Sizhou forms a mutual stronghold—not easily seized at a stroke.

sentences.zh: 海州、東海、石秋，遠在數百里之外，必不嚴備。

translations.literal: Haizhou, Donghai, and Shiqou lie hundreds of li away and will surely not be strictly guarded.
translations.idiomatic: Haizhou, Donghai, and Shiqou lie hundreds of li distant—they will not be heavily defended.

sentences.zh: 吾頓大兵為疑兵，以輕騎倍道襲之，其守將可擒也。」

translations.literal: I shall station the main force as a decoy and send light cavalry by forced march to strike them; their defending generals can be captured."
translations.idiomatic: I shall hold the main body here as a feint and send light horse by forced marches to strike them—their commanders can be taken."

sentences.zh: 師至，三城果皆下，清河亦降。

translations.literal: When the army arrived, the three cities were indeed all taken, and Qinghe also surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: The columns arrived; all three cities fell, and Qinghe surrendered as well.

sentences.zh: 宋主以國內附，而淮東諸城猶為之守。

translations.literal: The Song ruler had submitted the state, yet the cities of Huaidong still held out for him.
translations.idiomatic: The Song emperor had surrendered the realm, but the Huaidong towns still held for him.

sentences.zh: 詔博羅歡進軍，拔淮安南堡，戰白馬湖及寶應，掠高郵，自西小河入漕河，據灣頭，斷通、泰援兵，遂下揚州，淮東平。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Boluohuan to advance; he took Huai'an's southern fort, fought at Baima Lake and Baoying, raided Gaoyou, entered the Grand Canal from the West Small River, held Wantou, cut off reinforcements from Tong and Tai, then took Yangzhou, and Huaidong was pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Boluohuan was ordered forward. He took Huai'an's southern fort, fought at Baima Lake and Baoying, raided Gaoyou, entered the Grand Canal by the West Small River, seized Wantou, severed reinforcements from Tongzhou and Taizhou, and finally took Yangzhou—Huaidong was pacified.

sentences.zh: 益封桂陽、德慶二萬一千戶。

translations.literal: His enfeoffment was increased by twenty-one thousand households in Guiyang and Deqing.
translations.idiomatic: His fief was enlarged by twenty-one thousand households in Guiyang and Deqing.

sentences.zh: 十四年，討叛臣只裏斡臺於應昌，平之。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year he campaigned against the rebel minister Zhiliwotai at Yingchang and pacified him.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year he suppressed the rebel Zhiliwotai at Yingchang and restored order.

sentences.zh: 賜玉帶文綺，與博羅同署樞密院事，拜中書右丞，行省北京。

translations.literal: He was granted a jade belt and patterned silks, shared duties at the Bureau of Military Affairs with Boluo, was appointed Right Vice-Chancellor of the Central Secretariat, and served as regional commissioner for Beijing.
translations.idiomatic: He received a jade belt and brocade, shared Bureau of Military Affairs duties with Boluo, was made Right Vice-Chancellor of the Central Secretariat, and governed Beijing as regional commissioner.

sentences.zh: 未幾，召還。

translations.literal: Before long he was recalled.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was recalled to court.

sentences.zh: 時江南新附，尚多反側，詔募民能從大軍進討者，使自為一軍，聽節度於其長，而毋役於他軍，制命符節，皆與正同。

translations.literal: At that time the newly submitted Jiangnan region still harbored much unrest; an edict recruited civilians able to follow the great army in advance campaigns, made them form their own army, subject to the command of their own leader and not to service in other armies, with commissions, orders, and tally tokens all the same as for regular troops.
translations.idiomatic: The newly pacified south was still restless; the court recruited civilians willing to march with the main armies, formed them into separate units under their own leaders, exempt from service in other commands, with commissions and tally tokens equal to those of regular forces.

sentences.zh: 會博羅歡寢疾，乃附樞密董文忠奏曰：「今疆土浸廣，勝兵百萬，指揮可集，何假此無藉之徒。

translations.literal: Boluohuan happened to be bedridden with illness; he had the Bureau of Military Affairs officer Dong Wenzong attach a memorial saying, "The realm grows ever wider; a million victorious troops can be assembled at command—why rely on these rootless men?
translations.idiomatic: Boluohuan was then ill in bed; through Dong Wenzong of the Bureau of Military Affairs he memorialized, "The empire grows daily; a million trained soldiers stand ready—why employ these masterless rabble?

sentences.zh: 彼一踐南土，則掠人貨財，俘人妻孥，仇怨益滋，而叛者將愈眾矣。」

translations.literal: Once they set foot in the south, they will plunder people's goods and seize wives and children; grievances will only increase, and rebels will grow ever more numerous."
translations.idiomatic: Once they enter the south they will loot property and seize women and children; hatred will deepen and rebellion will spread."

sentences.zh: 奏上，召輿疾賜坐，與語，帝大悟，遂可其奏。

translations.literal: When the memorial was submitted, he was summoned though ill, granted a seat, and spoke with the emperor; the emperor greatly understood and approved the memorial.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial reached the throne; Boluohuan was summoned despite his illness, given a seat, and questioned. The emperor saw the force of it and approved.

sentences.zh: 而常德入訴唐兀一軍殘暴其境內，敕斬以徇。

translations.literal: Meanwhile Changde submitted a complaint that a Tangut army had ravaged its territory; an edict ordered the offenders beheaded as a public warning.
translations.idiomatic: Changde meanwhile petitioned that a Tangut unit had ravaged the prefecture; the emperor ordered the culprits beheaded as an example.

sentences.zh: 凡所募軍皆罷。

translations.literal: All the recruited armies were disbanded.
translations.idiomatic: All the recruited units were dissolved.

sentences.zh: 十六年，以哈剌斯、博羅思、斡羅罕諸部不相統，命博羅歡監之。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year, because the Qaras, Boros, and Olonhan tribes were not under unified command, Boluohuan was ordered to supervise them.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year, with the Qaras, Boros, and Olonhan tribes lacking unified leadership, Boluohuan was placed over them.

sentences.zh: 十八年，以中書右丞行省甘肅。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year he served as Right Vice-Chancellor of the Central Secretariat and regional commissioner of Gansu.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year he governed Gansu as Right Vice-Chancellor of the Central Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 二十年，拜御史大夫，行御史臺事，以疾歸。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year he was appointed Censor-in-Chief and directed the Censorate, then returned home because of illness.
translations.idiomatic: In the twentieth year he was made Censor-in-Chief and head of the Censorate, but retired ill.

sentences.zh: 諸王乃顏叛，帝將親征。

translations.literal: Prince Nayan rebelled, and the emperor was about to campaign in person.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Nayan rebelled, the emperor prepared to take the field himself.

sentences.zh: 博羅歡諫曰：「昔太祖分封東諸侯，其地與戶，臣皆知之，以二十為率，乃顏得其九，忙兀、兀魯、紥剌兒、弘吉剌、亦其烈思五諸侯得其十一，惟征五諸侯兵，自足當之，何至上煩乘輿哉？

translations.literal: Boluohuan remonstrated, saying, "Formerly the Founder enfeoffed the eastern feudatories; I know their lands and households. Taking twenty as the whole, Nayan holds nine parts; the five feudatories Mangwu, Uriangqai, Jala'ir, Hongjila, and Yiqiliesi hold eleven parts among them. Summon only the troops of the five feudatories and they will suffice—why trouble the imperial carriage to go in person?
translations.idiomatic: Boluohuan urged against it: "When the Founder enfeoffed the eastern princes, I knew every grant of land and households. Of twenty parts in all, Nayan holds nine; Mangwu, Uriangqai, the Jala'ir, the Hongjila, and the Yiqiliesi hold eleven among them. The five princes' armies alone are enough—why should the Son of Heaven take the field?

sentences.zh: 臣疾且愈，請事東征。」

translations.literal: Your servant's illness is nearly cured; I request to undertake the eastern campaign."
translations.idiomatic: My illness is nearly past; let me lead the eastern campaign."

sentences.zh: 帝乃賜鎧甲弓矢鞍勒，命督五諸侯兵，與乃顏戰，敗之。

translations.literal: The emperor then bestowed armor, bow and arrows, and saddle and bridle, ordered him to command the troops of the five feudatories, fought Nayan, and defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor gave him armor, bow, arrows, saddle, and bridle, and ordered him to lead the five princes' forces against Nayan and defeat him—which he did.

sentences.zh: 其黨塔不帶以兵來拒，會久雨，軍乏食，諸將欲退。

translations.literal: Nayan's follower Tabudai came with troops to resist; prolonged rain fell, the army lacked food, and the generals wished to withdraw.
translations.idiomatic: Nayan's lieutenant Tabudai marched to oppose him; rains dragged on, provisions ran short, and the commanders wanted to pull back.

sentences.zh: 博羅歡曰：「今兩陣相對，豈容先動？」

translations.literal: Boluohuan said, "The two battle lines now face each other—how can we be the first to move?"
translations.idiomatic: Boluohuan said, "Two armies face each other across the field—who dares break first?"

sentences.zh: 俄塔不帶引兵退。

translations.literal: Soon Tabudai withdrew his troops.
translations.idiomatic: Presently Tabudai drew off his force.

sentences.zh: 博羅歡以其師乘之，轉戰二日，身中三矢，大破之，斬其駙馬忽倫。

translations.literal: Boluohuan pursued with his army, fought for two days, took three arrows in his body, routed the enemy utterly, and beheaded Tabudai's son-in-law Hulun.
translations.idiomatic: Boluohuan pressed the pursuit; two days of fighting left him with three arrow wounds, but the enemy was routed and Tabudai's son-in-law Hulun was slain.

sentences.zh: 適太師月魯那演大軍來會，遂平乃顏，擒塔不帶。

translations.literal: Just then Grand Preceptor Yelunayan's great army arrived and joined him; Nayan was then pacified and Tabudai captured.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Preceptor Yelunayan's main army then joined him; Nayan was crushed and Tabudai taken.

sentences.zh: 既而其黨哈丹復叛，詔與諸侯王乃馬帶討之。

translations.literal: Afterward his follower Hadan rebelled again; an edict ordered Boluohuan to campaign against him together with the feudal prince Naimadai.
translations.idiomatic: Hadan, another of Nayan's followers, rose again; Boluohuan was ordered to suppress him with Prince Naimadai.

sentences.zh: 哈丹遊騎猝至，博羅歡從三騎返走，抵絕澗，可二丈許，追騎垂及，博羅歡策其馬一躍而過，三從騎皆沒，人以為有神助云。

translations.literal: Hadan's scouting cavalry suddenly arrived; Boluohuan fled back with three riders, reached a sheer ravine about two zhang wide, and with pursuers close behind, Boluohuan spurred his horse and leaped across in one bound; the three followers all drowned, and people said he had divine aid.
translations.idiomatic: Hadan's scouts suddenly appeared; Boluohuan turned back with three companions and came to a ravine some two zhang across, pursuers at his heels. He spurred his horse and cleared it in a single leap; all three followers were lost in the gorge, and men said heaven had helped him.

sentences.zh: 哈丹死，斬其子老的於陣。

translations.literal: Hadan died; his son Laodi was beheaded on the battlefield.
translations.idiomatic: Hadan fell; his son Laodi was slain in battle.

sentences.zh: 往返凡四歲。

translations.literal: The round trip took four years in all.
translations.idiomatic: The campaign there and back took four years.

sentences.zh: 凱旋，俘哈丹二妃以獻，敕以一賜乃馬帶，一賜博羅歡。

translations.literal: Returning in triumph, he captured Hadan's two consorts and presented them; an edict gave one to Naimadai and one to Boluohuan.
translations.idiomatic: Returning in triumph, he presented Hadan's two consorts as captives; one was given to Naimadai and one to Boluohuan.

sentences.zh: 陳其金銀器於延春閣，上召諸侯王將帥分賜之。

translations.literal: The gold and silver vessels were displayed in the Yanchun Pavilion; the sovereign summoned the feudal princes and generals to divide and bestow them.
translations.idiomatic: Gold and silver vessels were laid out in the Yanchun Pavilion, and the emperor summoned princes and commanders to divide them.

sentences.zh: 博羅歡辭，帝曰：「卿可謂能讓。」

translations.literal: Boluohuan declined; the emperor said, "You may truly be called capable of yielding."
translations.idiomatic: Boluohuan refused his share; the emperor said, "You know how to yield."

sentences.zh: 乃賜金銀器五百兩以旌之。

translations.literal: He was then granted five hundred taels' worth of gold and silver vessels in commendation.
translations.idiomatic: He was rewarded with gold and silver vessels worth five hundred taels in recognition.

sentences.zh: 河南宣慰改行中書省，拜平章政事，有詔括馬毋及勛臣之家。

translations.literal: The Henan pacification commission was converted to a Branch Secretariat; he was appointed Grand Councillor, and an edict requisitioned horses but was not to extend to the households of meritorious ministers.
translations.idiomatic: When Henan's pacification office became a Branch Secretariat, he was made Grand Councillor; an edict requisitioned horses but exempted the households of meritorious ministers.

sentences.zh: 博羅歡曰：「吾馬成群，所治地方三千里，不先出馬，何以為吏民之倡？」

translations.literal: Boluohuan said, "My horses run in herds; the territory I govern spans three thousand li—if I do not offer horses first, how can I lead officials and people by example?"
translations.idiomatic: Boluohuan said, "My herds are vast and my province spans three thousand li—if I do not lead with my own horses, how can I ask others to follow?"

sentences.zh: 乃先入善馬十有八。

translations.literal: He then first submitted eighteen fine horses.
translations.idiomatic: He was first to submit eighteen good horses.

sentences.zh: 汴南諸州，漭為巨浸，博羅歡躬行決口，督有司繕完之。

translations.literal: The prefectures south of Bian had become a vast flood; Boluohuan went in person to open the breach and supervised the relevant offices in repairing it.
translations.idiomatic: South of Bian the prefectures lay under vast floods; Boluohuan went in person to open the breach and saw the repairs through.

sentences.zh: 三十一年，成宗立，遷陜西行中書省平章政事。

translations.literal: In the thirty-first year, when Chengzong acceded, he was transferred to be Grand Councillor of the Shaanxi Branch Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-first year, when Chengzong took the throne, he was transferred to Grand Councillor of the Shaanxi Branch Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 未行，留鎮河南。

translations.literal: Before he departed, he was retained to garrison Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Before he could leave, he was kept to govern Henan.

sentences.zh: 入朝，請以泰安州所入五戶絲四千斤易內庫繒帛，分給忙兀一軍。

translations.literal: At audience at court, he requested to exchange four thousand jin of the five-household silk tribute from Taian prefecture for palace silks and distribute them to the Mangwu army.
translations.idiomatic: At court he asked to exchange four thousand jin of Taian's five-household silk tribute for palace brocade and distribute it among the Mangwu troops.

sentences.zh: 帝為敕遞車送軍中，賜以銀百五十兩。

translations.literal: The emperor issued an edict that relay carts deliver it to the army and granted him one hundred fifty taels of silver.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered relay wagons to carry the goods to camp and gave him one hundred fifty taels of silver.

sentences.zh: 陛辭，帝諭之曰：「卿今白須，世祖德言，實多聞之，宜加慎護。」

translations.literal: At farewell audience the emperor instructed him, saying, "Your beard is white now; you heard much of Kublai's virtuous words—take good care of yourself."
translations.idiomatic: Taking leave of the throne, the emperor told him, "Your beard is white now; you heard much of Kublai's counsel—guard your health."

sentences.zh: 因以世祖所佩弓矢鞶帶賜之。

translations.literal: He then bestowed upon him the bow, arrows, and belt Kublai had worn.
translations.idiomatic: He then gave him the bow, arrows, and belt Kublai had worn.

sentences.zh: 有頃，近臣奏：「伐宋時，右軍分屬伯顏、阿術，左軍分屬博羅歡。

translations.literal: Before long a close attendant memorialized, "When Song was attacked, the right wing was divided between Bayan and Aju, the left wing between Boluohuan.
translations.idiomatic: Soon a court favorite memorialized, "In the Song campaign the right wing was divided between Bayan and Aju, the left between Boluohuan alone.

sentences.zh: 今伯顏、阿術皆受分地，而博羅歡未及，惟帝裁之。」

translations.literal: Now Bayan and Aju have both received allotted lands, but Boluohuan has not yet received his; may the emperor decide."
translations.idiomatic: Bayan and Aju have both received fiefs, but Boluohuan has not—let the throne decide."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「何久不言，豈彼恥自請耶？」

translations.literal: The emperor said, "Why was this not spoken of long ago—was he ashamed to ask for himself?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Why was this never raised—was he too proud to ask?"

sentences.zh: 乃益封高郵五百戶。

translations.literal: He then increased his enfeoffment by five hundred households in Gaoyou.
translations.idiomatic: He then added five hundred Gaoyou households to his fief.

sentences.zh: 大德元年，叛王藥木忽兒、兀魯速不花來歸。

translations.literal: In the first year of Dade, the rebel princes Yaqumuqur and Ulus Buqa came to submit.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Dade the rebel princes Yaqumuqur and Ulus Buqa returned to allegiance.

sentences.zh: 博羅歡聞之，遣使馳奏曰：「諸王之叛，皆由其父，此輩幼弱，無所與知。今茲來歸，宜棄其前惡，以勸未至。」

translations.literal: Boluohuan heard of it and sent a fast messenger to memorialize: "The princes' rebellion was all due to their fathers; these are young and weak and had no part in knowing it. Now that they have come to submit, their former wrongs should be set aside to encourage those who have not yet come."
translations.idiomatic: When Boluohuan heard this, he sent a fast courier to memorialize: "The princes rebelled only because of their fathers; these are young and had no part in it. Now that they have returned, their past offenses should be set aside to encourage those still holding out."

sentences.zh: 帝深以為然，賜金鞍勒，命以平章政事行省湖廣。

translations.literal: The Emperor deeply approved, granted a golden saddle and bridle, and appointed him Associate Director of the Secretariat administering the Huguang Branch Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor fully agreed, granted him a golden saddle and bridle, and appointed him associate director of the Secretariat with charge of the Huguang Branch Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 會并福建行省入江浙，拜光祿大夫、上柱國、江浙等處行中書省平章政事。

translations.literal: When Fujian Branch Secretariat was merged into Zhejiang and Jiangsu, he was appointed Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, Senior Pillar of State, and Associate Director of the Branch Secretariat of Zhejiang and Jiangsu.
translations.idiomatic: When the Fujian Branch Secretariat was merged into Jiangsu and Zhejiang, he was appointed Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, Senior Pillar of State, and Associate Director of the Jiangsu and Zhejiang Branch Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 居歲餘，卒，年六十三。

translations.literal: After a little more than a year he died, aged sixty-three.
translations.idiomatic: A little over a year later he died, aged sixty-three.

sentences.zh: 博羅歡勇有智略，戰常以身先之，所獲財物悉與將士，故得其死力。

translations.literal: Boluohuan was brave and possessed strategic insight; in battle he always took the lead in person; all goods and wealth captured he entirely shared with officers and soldiers, thus obtaining their utmost loyalty unto death.
translations.idiomatic: Boluohuan was brave and shrewd; in battle he always led from the front, sharing every prize with his officers and men—and so won their loyalty unto death.

sentences.zh: 平居常以國事為憂，聞變即請行，至終其事乃止。

translations.literal: In ordinary times he constantly took state affairs as his worry; hearing of emergency he immediately requested to go; only when the affair was finished to the end did he stop.
translations.idiomatic: In daily life he was constantly troubled by affairs of state; at word of crisis he would immediately ask to go—and would not rest until the matter was seen through.

sentences.zh: 其忠義蓋天性然也。

translations.literal: His loyalty and righteousness were surely his inborn nature.
translations.idiomatic: His loyalty and righteousness were surely innate.

sentences.zh: 累贈推忠宣力贊運功臣、太師、開府儀同三司、上柱國，加封泰安王，謚武穆。

translations.literal: Posthumously repeatedly enfeoffed as Meritorious Minister Who Pushes Loyalty and Declares Strength to Support the Dynasty, Grand Preceptor, Grand General of State with Ceremonial Honors Equal to the Three Excellencies, Senior Pillar of State; additionally enfeoffed as Prince of Tai'an; posthumous name Wumu.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumously he was repeatedly ennobled as Meritorious Minister of Loyalty and Supporting Effort, Grand Preceptor, Grand General of State with the Ceremonial Standing of the Three Excellencies, and Senior Pillar of State; he was further enfeoffed Prince of Tai'an, with the posthumous name Wumu, Establisher of Martial Achievement.

sentences.zh: 子渾都、伯都、野先帖木兒、博羅。

translations.literal: His sons were Hundu, Bedu, Yexiantie'er, and Boluo.
translations.idiomatic: His sons were Hundu, Bedu, Yexiantie'er, and Boluo.

sentences.zh: 渾都，山東宣慰使，遙授中書平章政事。

translations.literal: Hundu was Pacification Commissioner of Shandong and remotely appointed Associate Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Hundu served as Pacification Commissioner of Shandong and held the remote appointment of Associate Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 野先帖木兒，河南江北等處行中書省左丞相。

translations.literal: Yexiantie'er was Left Grand Councillor of the Branch Secretariat of Henan and the Northern Yangtze, etc.
translations.idiomatic: Yexiantie'er was Left Grand Councillor of the Branch Secretariat for Henan and the Northern Yangtze region.

sentences.zh: 卒官開府儀同三司、翰林學士承旨。

translations.literal: He died in office as Grand General of State with Ceremonial Honors Equal to the Three Excellencies and Academician Expositor-in-Chief of the Hanlin Academy.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office as Grand General of State with the Ceremonial Standing of the Three Excellencies and Expositor-in-Chief of the Hanlin Academy.

sentences.zh: 博羅，陜西等處行中書省平章政事。

translations.literal: Boluo was Associate Director of the Branch Secretariat of Shaanxi, etc.
translations.idiomatic: Boluo was Associate Director of the Branch Secretariat for Shaanxi and neighboring circuits.

sentences.zh: 野先帖木兒子尼摩星吉，襲郡王；

translations.literal: Yexiantie'er's son Nimoxingji inherited the title of Commandery Prince;
translations.idiomatic: Yexiantie'er's son Nimoxingji inherited the title of Commandery Prince;

sentences.zh: 亦思剌瓦性吉，中政使。

translations.literal: Yisilawaxingji was Director of the Central Affairs Office.
translations.idiomatic: Yisilawaxingji served as Director of the Central Affairs Office.

sentences.zh: 伯都幼穎異，不以家世自矜，長嗜書史。

translations.literal: Bedu in youth was precocious and exceptional; he did not pride himself on his family status; growing up he was devoted to books and history.
translations.idiomatic: Bedu was unusually bright as a child and never prided himself on his lineage; as he grew he devoured books and history.

sentences.zh: 大德五年，擢江東道廉訪副使，拜江南行臺侍御史。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Dade, he was selected as Vice Commissioner of the Circuit Intendant for Integrity of the Jiandong Circuit and appointed Attending Censor of the Jiangnan Branch Censorate.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Dade he was promoted to Vice Commissioner of the Jiandong Circuit Intendant for Integrity and appointed Attending Censor of the Jiangnan Branch Censorate.

sentences.zh: 未幾，召入僉樞密院事，領舍兒別赤。

translations.literal: Before long he was summoned to serve as Assistant Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs and to lead the Chernih Bichig.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was recalled to serve as Assistant Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs and to head the Chernih Bichig.

sentences.zh: 至大二年，出為江南行臺御史中丞，遷陜西行臺御史大夫。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhida, he was dispatched as Vice Censor-in-Chief of the Jiangnan Branch Censorate and transferred to Grand Censor of the Shaanxi Branch Censorate.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Zhida he was sent out as Vice Censor-in-Chief of the Jiangnan Branch Censorate, then moved to Grand Censor of the Shaanxi Branch Censorate.

sentences.zh: 延祐元年，拜甘肅行省平章政事。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yanyou, he was appointed Associate Director of the Gansu Branch Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Yanyou he was appointed Associate Director of the Gansu Branch Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 時米價騰湧，陸挽一石，費二百緡，乃為經畫計，所省至四百餘萬緡，自是諸倉俱充溢。

translations.literal: At the time rice prices surged; transporting one shi overland cost two hundred strings of cash; he then devised a plan; what was saved reached over four million strings; from then on all granaries were fully overflowing.
translations.idiomatic: Rice prices were soaring; hauling one shi overland cost two hundred strings of cash. Bedu worked out a scheme that saved more than four million strings, and from then on every granary was full.

sentences.zh: 甘州氣寒地瘠，少稔歲。

translations.literal: Ganzhou's climate was cold and the land barren; few years had good harvests.
translations.idiomatic: Ganzhou was cold and its soil poor, with few years of good harvest.

sentences.zh: 民饑，則發粟賑之，春闕種，則貸之。

translations.literal: When the people suffered famine, he released grain to relieve them; when in spring they lacked seed, he loaned it to them.
translations.idiomatic: When the people went hungry he opened the granaries; when they lacked seed in spring he lent it to them.

sentences.zh: 於是兵餉既足，民食亦給。

translations.literal: Thereupon military provisions were sufficient and the people's food was also supplied.
translations.idiomatic: Military rations were made good and the people's food needs were met.

sentences.zh: 詔賜名鷹、甲胄、弓矢及鈔五千緡以勞焉。

translations.literal: An edict granted him a named hawk, armor, bow and arrows, and five thousand strings of paper money to reward him.
translations.idiomatic: An edict rewarded him with a named hawk, armor, bow and arrows, and five thousand strings of paper money.

sentences.zh: 四年，移江浙行省平章政事，入為太子賓客。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he was transferred to Associate Director of the Zhejiang Branch Secretariat and entered the capital as Tutor to the Crown Prince.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he was transferred to Associate Director of the Zhejiang Branch Secretariat and recalled to the capital as Tutor to the Crown Prince.

sentences.zh: 上書陳古先聖王正心修身之道，帝嘉納之。

translations.literal: He submitted a memorial setting forth the ways by which ancient sage kings rectified the heart and cultivated the self; the Emperor praised and accepted it.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized the court on how the ancient sage kings rectified the heart and cultivated the self; the Emperor praised and adopted his advice.

sentences.zh: 遷江南行臺御史大夫。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Grand Censor of the Jiangnan Branch Censorate.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Grand Censor of the Jiangnan Branch Censorate.

sentences.zh: 皇太后謂東宮官不宜使外，止其行。

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager said that Eastern Palace officials should not be sent outside; his departure was stopped.
translations.idiomatic: The Empress Dowager held that officials of the Eastern Palace should not be posted outside the capital, and his transfer was halted.

sentences.zh: 遂以疾辭去，寓居高郵。

translations.literal: He then resigned on grounds of illness and took up residence in Gaoyou.
translations.idiomatic: He then resigned, pleading illness, and made his home in Gaoyou.

sentences.zh: 英宗即位，復命為江南行臺御史大夫。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yingzong took the throne, he was again appointed Grand Censor of the Jiangnan Branch Censorate.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yingzong ascended the throne, Bedu was again appointed Grand Censor of the Jiangnan Branch Censorate.

sentences.zh: 陛見，以疾固辭。

translations.literal: On audience at court he firmly declined on grounds of illness.
translations.idiomatic: At his audience he steadfastly pleaded illness and declined.

sentences.zh: 帝慰諭久之，命以平章之祿歸養於家，復賜鈔十萬緡。

translations.literal: The Emperor comforted and admonished him at length, ordered that he be sent home on the salary of an Associate Director to recuperate, and again granted him one hundred thousand strings of paper money.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor comforted him at length, ordered him home on an associate director's salary to convalesce, and again granted him one hundred thousand strings of paper money.

sentences.zh: 所服藥須空青，詔遣使江南訪求之。

translations.literal: The medicine he took required malachite; an edict dispatched envoys to Jiangnan to seek it.
translations.idiomatic: The medicine he required called for malachite; an edict sent envoys to Jiangnan to obtain it.

sentences.zh: 伯都辭謝曰：「臣曩膺重寄，深懼弗稱，今已病廢，況敢叨濫厚祿以受重賜乎？」

translations.literal: Bedu declined and thanked him, saying: "Your subject formerly received weighty commission and deeply feared he was unworthy; now I am disabled by illness—how much more would I dare to accept lavish salary and heavy gifts in excess?"
translations.idiomatic: Bedu declined, saying, "I once bore a heavy charge and feared I was not equal to it; now I am broken by illness—how dare I accept a lavish salary and rich gifts besides?"

sentences.zh: 並以所給平章政事祿歸有司。

translations.literal: He also returned to the relevant office the salary of Associate Director of the Secretariat that had been granted him.
translations.idiomatic: He also returned the associate director's salary that had been granted him to the appropriate office.

sentences.zh: 泰定元年，還京師，卒。

translations.literal: In the first year of Taiding he returned to the capital and died.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Taiding he returned to the capital and died.

sentences.zh: 朝廷知其貧，賻鈔二萬五千貫。

translations.literal: The court knew he was poor and gave funeral gifts of twenty-five thousand strings of paper money.
translations.idiomatic: The court, knowing he was poor, granted twenty-five thousand strings in funeral compensation.

sentences.zh: 御史臺奏賻三萬五千貫，仍還所辭祿，妻弘吉剌氏弗受，曰：「始伯都仕於朝，不敢虛受廩祿。

translations.literal: The Censorate memorialized for funeral gifts of thirty-five thousand strings and also to return the salary he had declined; his wife Lady Hongjila refused, saying: "When Bedu first served at court, he did not dare receive salary without merit.
translations.idiomatic: The Censorate recommended thirty-five thousand strings in funeral gifts and the return of the salary he had declined; his wife, Lady Hongjila, refused, saying, "When Bedu first entered service he would not take salary he had not earned.

sentences.zh: 今歿矣，茍受是祿，非其意也。」

translations.literal: Now that he is dead, if I accept this salary it would be against his intent."
translations.idiomatic: Now that he is gone, to accept this salary would go against his wishes."

sentences.zh: 卒辭之。

translations.literal: She finally declined it.
translations.idiomatic: In the end she refused it.

sentences.zh: 子篤爾只，將作院判官。

translations.literal: His son Duerzhi was Vice-Director of the Directorate of Palace Construction.
translations.idiomatic: His son Duerzhi was Vice-Director of the Directorate of Palace Construction.

sentences.zh: ○抄思

translations.literal: ○ Chaosi
translations.idiomatic: ○ Chaosi

sentences.zh: 抄思，乃蠻部人。

translations.literal: Chaosi was a man of the Naiman tribe.
translations.idiomatic: Chaosi was a man of the Naiman tribe.

sentences.zh: 又號曰答祿。

translations.literal: He was also styled Dalu.
translations.idiomatic: He was also known as Dalu.

sentences.zh: 其先泰陽，為乃蠻部主。

translations.literal: His ancestor was Taiyang, chieftain of the Naiman tribe.
translations.idiomatic: His ancestor Taiyang had been chieftain of the Naiman tribe.

sentences.zh: 祖曲書律。

translations.literal: His grandfather was Qushulu.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather was Qushulu.

sentences.zh: 父敞溫。

translations.literal: His father was Changwen.
translations.idiomatic: His father was Changwen.

sentences.zh: 太祖舉兵討不庭，曲書律失其部落，敞溫奔契丹卒。

translations.literal: When the Taizu raised troops to punish the rebellious, Qushulu lost his tribe; Changwen fled to the Khitan and died there.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizu raised troops to punish rebels, Qushulu lost his tribe; Changwen fled to the Khitan and died there.

sentences.zh: 抄思尚幼，與其母跋涉間行，歸太祖，奉中宮旨侍宮掖。

translations.literal: Chaosi was still young; with his mother he traveled by difficult paths and came to the Taizu; following the Central Palace's order he served in the inner palace quarters.
translations.idiomatic: Chaosi was still a child; he and his mother made their way by secret and arduous routes to Taizu, and by order of the Central Palace served in the inner quarters.

sentences.zh: 抄思年二十五，即從征伐，破代、石二州，不避矢石，每先登焉。

translations.literal: When Chaosi was twenty-five he immediately followed on campaigns; he captured the two prefectures of Dai and Shi, not avoiding arrows and stones, always climbing first.
translations.idiomatic: At twenty-five Chaosi joined the campaigns, stormed the prefectures of Dai and Shi, never flinching from arrow or stone, and was always first over the wall.

sentences.zh: 雁門之戰，屢捷。

translations.literal: In the battles at Yanmen he repeatedly won victories.
translations.idiomatic: At Yanmen he won victory again and again.

sentences.zh: 會太宗命睿宗平金，抄思執銳以從，與金兵戰，所向無前。

translations.literal: When Taizong ordered Ruizong to pacify Jin, Chaosi grasped sharp weapons and followed; fighting Jin troops, wherever he went none could stand before him.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizong ordered Ruizong to pacify the Jin, Chaosi took up arms and followed; against Jin forces he was irresistible wherever he fought.

sentences.zh: 壬辰，兵次鈞州，金兵壘於三峰山，抄思察其營壁不堅，夜領精騎襲之，金兵驚擾，遂乘擊之，拔三峰山。

translations.literal: In the year renchen the army halted at Jun Prefecture; Jin troops fortified at Sanfeng Mountain; Chaosi observed their camp walls were not solid; at night he led elite cavalry to raid them; the Jin troops were alarmed and thrown into disorder; he then seized the moment to attack and took Sanfeng Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: In renchen the army halted at Jun Prefecture while Jin troops fortified Sanfeng Mountain. Chaosi saw their walls were weak; at night he led elite cavalry in a raid, threw the Jin camp into panic, pressed the attack, and took the mountain.

sentences.zh: 睿宗以抄思功聞於朝，有旨以湯陰縣黃招撫等一百一十七戶賜之。

translations.literal: Ruizong reported Chaosi's achievement to the court; there was an imperial order granting him one hundred seventeen households including pacification commissioner Huang of Tangyin County.
translations.idiomatic: Ruizong reported Chaosi's feat to court; an edict granted him one hundred seventeen households, including Pacification Commissioner Huang of Tangyin County.

sentences.zh: 抄思力辭不受。

translations.literal: Chaosi forcefully declined and would not accept.
translations.idiomatic: Chaosi firmly refused.

sentences.zh: 復賜以男女五十口，宅一區，黃金鞶帶、酒壺、杯盂各一。

translations.literal: He was again granted fifty male and female servants, one residence, and one each of golden belt plaque, wine kettle, and cups and bowls.
translations.idiomatic: He was given instead fifty male and female servants, a residence, and one each of a golden belt plaque, wine kettle, and cups and bowls.

sentences.zh: 辭弗許，乃受之。

translations.literal: Declining was not permitted, so he accepted.
translations.idiomatic: Refusal was not allowed, and he accepted.

sentences.zh: 制授萬戶，與內侍胡都虎、留乞簽起西京等處軍人征行及鎮守隨州。

translations.literal: By decree he was appointed commander of ten thousand, wanhu, and together with the inner attendant Huduhu and Liuqi signed orders to mobilize and garrison troops from the Western Capital and other places for campaigns and to garrison Suizhou.
translations.idiomatic: By imperial order he was made wanhu; together with the inner attendant Huduhu and Liuqi he signed orders mobilizing troops from the Western Capital and elsewhere for campaigns and to garrison Suizhou.

sentences.zh: 招集民戶，每千人以官一員領之。

translations.literal: He gathered civilian households; for every thousand people one official was appointed to lead them.
translations.idiomatic: He gathered civilian households, appointing one official to lead every thousand persons.

sentences.zh: 丁酉秋七月，奉旨調軍，得西京、大名、濱、棣、懷、孟、真定、河間、邢、名、磁、威、新、衛、保等府州軍四千六十餘人，統之。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of autumn in the year dingyou, following an imperial order to mobilize troops, he obtained over four thousand sixty men from the military units of the prefectures and circuits of the Western Capital, Daming, Bin, Di, Huai, Meng, Zhending, Hejian, Xing, Ming, Ci, Wei, Xin, Wei, Bao, and others, and took overall command.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of dingyou, under orders to mobilize troops, he mustered more than four thousand sixty men from the Western Capital, Daming, Bin, Di, Huai, Meng, Zhending, Hejian, Xing, Ming, Ci, Wei, Xin, Wei, Bao, and other prefectures and circuits, and took command of them all.

sentences.zh: 後移鎮潁，以疾歸大名。

translations.literal: Later he was transferred to garrison at Ying and returned to Daming because of illness.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was transferred to garrison Yingzhou, then returned to Daming on account of illness.

sentences.zh: 歲戊申正月卒，年四十四。

translations.literal: In the first month of the year wushen he died, aged forty-four.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of wushen he died, aged forty-four.

sentences.zh: 子別的因。

translations.literal: His son was Biedeyin.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Biedeyin.

sentences.zh: 別的因在繈褓時，父抄思方領兵平金，與其祖母康裏氏在三皇后宮庭。

translations.literal: When Biedeyin was in swaddling clothes, his father Chaosi was leading troops to pacify Jin; he and his grandmother Lady Kangli were in the court of the Three Empresses.
translations.idiomatic: While Biedeyin was still in swaddling clothes, his father Chaosi was leading troops against the Jin; he and his grandmother Lady Kangli lived in the Three Empresses' palace.

sentences.zh: 戊申，父抄思卒，母張氏迎別的因以歸。

translations.literal: In wushen his father Chaosi died; his mother Lady Zhang went to receive Biedeyin and bring him home.
translations.idiomatic: In wushen his father Chaosi died; his mother Lady Zhang went to fetch Biedeyin and bring him home.

sentences.zh: 祖母康裏氏卒。

translations.literal: His grandmother Lady Kangli died.
translations.idiomatic: His grandmother Lady Kangli died.

sentences.zh: 張嘗從容訓之曰：「人有三成人，知畏懼成人，知羞恥成人，知艱難成人。

translations.literal: Zhang once calmly instructed him: "A man becomes fully human in three ways: knowing fear and restraint makes one human, knowing shame makes one human, knowing hardship makes one human.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Zhang once gently admonished him: "There are three ways to become a fully human being: to know fear and restraint is to become human; to know shame is to become human; to know hardship is to become human.

sentences.zh: 否則禽獸而已。」

translations.literal: Otherwise one is merely a beast."
translations.idiomatic: Otherwise one is no better than a beast."

sentences.zh: 別的因受教唯謹。

translations.literal: Biedeyin received the instruction with utmost respect.
translations.idiomatic: Biedeyin took the lesson to heart and obeyed it scrupulously.

sentences.zh: 甲寅，世祖以宗王鎮黑水，有旨諭察罕那顏，命別的因襲抄思職，為副萬戶，鎮守隨、潁等處。

translations.literal: In jiayin Kublai, as imperial prince, was stationed at the Black Water; there was an order instructing Chahan Nayan to have Biedeyin inherit Chaosi's post as deputy wanhu, garrisoning Suizhou, Yingzhou, and other places.
translations.idiomatic: In jiayin Kublai, as an imperial prince, held the Black Water; an edict instructed Chahan Nayan to have Biedeyin inherit Chaosi's appointment as deputy wanhu, garrisoning Suizhou, Ying, and neighboring posts.

sentences.zh: 丙辰冬十有二月，世祖復諭征鎮軍士悉聽別的因等號令。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month of winter in bingchen Kublai again ordered that all campaign and garrison troops obey the commands of Biedeyin and others.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month of bingchen Kublai again ordered that all troops on campaign and garrison duty were to obey Biedeyin and his associates.

sentences.zh: 別的因身長七尺餘，肩豐多力，善刀舞，尤精騎射，士卒咸畏服之。

translations.literal: Biedeyin was over seven chi in height, broad-shouldered and very strong; skilled at sword dance and especially expert in mounted archery; officers and soldiers all feared and respected him.
translations.idiomatic: Biedeyin stood more than seven chi tall, with broad shoulders and great strength; he was skilled at sword dance and especially expert in mounted archery, and officers and soldiers alike feared and obeyed him.

sentences.zh: 明年，庚申，世祖即位，委任尤專。

translations.literal: The next year, gengshen, Kublai ascended the throne and entrusted him with still greater authority.
translations.idiomatic: The following year, gengshen, Kublai took the throne and entrusted him with even greater authority.

sentences.zh: 癸亥正月，召赴行在所。

translations.literal: In the first month of guihai he was summoned to the mobile imperial court.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of guihai he was summoned to the mobile court.

sentences.zh: 冬十一月，謁見世祖於行在所，世祖賜金符，以別的因為壽潁二州屯田府達魯花赤。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of winter he had audience with Kublai at the mobile court; Kublai granted him a golden tally and appointed Biedeyin darughachi of the Military Colony Office of Shou and Ying Prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month he had audience with Kublai at the mobile court; Kublai granted him a golden tally and appointed him darughachi of the Military Colony Office of Shou and Ying Prefectures.

sentences.zh: 時二州地多荒蕪，有虎食民妻，其夫來告，別的因默然良久，曰：「此易治耳。」

translations.literal: At the time much land in the two prefectures lay abandoned; a tiger ate a man's wife, and the husband came to report it. Biedeyin was silent for a long while and said: "This is easy to handle."
translations.idiomatic: Much land in the two prefectures lay fallow; a tiger had devoured a man's wife, and the husband came to report it. Biedeyin was silent a long while, then said, "This is easily dealt with."

sentences.zh: 乃立檻設機，縛羔羊檻中以誘虎。

translations.literal: He then set up a cage with a trigger mechanism and tied a lamb inside the cage to lure the tiger.
translations.idiomatic: He erected a cage with a spring trap and tied a lamb inside to bait the tiger.

sentences.zh: 夜半，虎果至，機發，虎墮檻中，因取射之，虎遂死。

translations.literal: At midnight the tiger indeed came; the mechanism tripped and the tiger fell into the cage; he then took aim and shot it, and the tiger died.
translations.idiomatic: At midnight the tiger came; the trap sprang and the tiger fell into the cage; he shot it and the tiger died.

sentences.zh: 自是虎害頓息。

translations.literal: From then on tiger attacks ceased abruptly.
translations.idiomatic: After that, tiger attacks ceased entirely.

sentences.zh: 至元十三年，授明威將軍、信陽府達魯花赤，佩金符。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year of Zhiyuan he was appointed General of Illustrious Might and darughachi of Xinyang Prefecture, wearing a golden tally.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year of Zhiyuan he was appointed General of Illustrious Might and darughachi of Xinyang Prefecture, with a golden tally.

sentences.zh: 時信陽亦多虎，別的因至未久，一日，以馬裼置鞍上出獵，命左右燔山，虎出走，別的因以裼擲虎，虎搏裼，據地而吼，別的因旋馬視虎射之，虎立死。

translations.literal: At the time Xinyang also had many tigers; not long after Biedeyin arrived, one day he went hunting with a horse blanket placed on the saddle, ordered his attendants to burn the hills, the tiger fled; Biedeyin threw the blanket at the tiger; the tiger fought the blanket, crouched on the ground and roared; Biedeyin wheeled his horse, fixed his gaze on the tiger and shot it, and the tiger died on the spot.
translations.idiomatic: Xinyang too was plagued by tigers. Not long after Biedeyin arrived, he went hunting one day with a horse blanket draped over the saddle, ordered his men to set fire to the hills, and when a tiger bolted he flung the blanket at it; the tiger clawed at the blanket, dropped to the ground, and roared; Biedeyin wheeled his horse, took aim, and shot—the tiger fell dead on the spot.

sentences.zh: 十六年，進宣威將軍、常德路副達魯花赤。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year he was promoted to General of Propagating Might and Deputy Darughachi of Changde Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year he was promoted to General of Propagating Might and Deputy Darughachi of Changde Circuit.

sentences.zh: 會同知李明秀作亂，別的因請以單騎往招之，直抵賊壘，賊輕之，不設備。

translations.literal: When Vice Administrator Li Mingxiu rebelled, Biedeyin requested to go alone on horseback to summon him; he went straight to the rebel fort; the rebels treated him lightly and made no preparations.
translations.idiomatic: When Vice Administrator Li Mingxiu rose in rebellion, Biedeyin asked leave to ride alone to summon him; he went straight to the rebel camp, which dismissed him and made no preparation.

sentences.zh: 別的因諭以朝廷恩德，使為自新計，明秀素畏服，遂與俱來。

translations.literal: Biedeyin expounded the court's grace and virtue and urged him to plan his own reform; Mingxiu had always feared and respected him, and thus came together with him.
translations.idiomatic: Biedeyin spoke of the court's grace and urged Mingxiu to find a way to redeem himself; Mingxiu, who had long feared and respected him, went back with him.

sentences.zh: 別的因聞於朝，明秀伏誅，賊遂平。

translations.literal: Biedeyin reported to the court; Mingxiu was executed, and the rebels were pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Biedeyin reported to court; Mingxiu was executed and the rebellion was suppressed.

sentences.zh: 三十一年，進懷遠大將軍，遷池州路達魯花赤。

translations.literal: In the thirty-first year he was promoted to Grand General of Cherishing the Remote and transferred to darughachi of Chizhou Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-first year he was promoted to Grand General Who Cherishes the Distant and transferred to darughachi of Chizhou Circuit.

sentences.zh: 之官，道經潁上。

translations.literal: On the way to take up his post he passed through Yingshang.
translations.idiomatic: On his way to take up office he passed through Yingshang.

sentences.zh: 潁近荊山，有野豕時出害民禾稼，民莫能制。

translations.literal: Ying is near Jing Mountain; wild boars sometimes emerged to harm the people's crops, and the people could not control them.
translations.idiomatic: Ying lies near Jing Mountain, where wild boars sometimes came out to ravage the people's crops, and none could stop them.

sentences.zh: 聞別的因至，迎拜境上，告以其故。

translations.literal: Hearing Biedeyin had arrived, they welcomed and bowed to him at the border and told him the reason.
translations.idiomatic: Learning that Biedeyin was coming, the people met him at the district border and told him why.

sentences.zh: 別的因曰：「毋慮也。」

translations.literal: Biedeyin said: "Do not worry."
translations.idiomatic: Biedeyin said, "Have no fear."

sentences.zh: 遂至荊山，以狼牙箭射之，豕走數里。

translations.literal: He then went to Jing Mountain and shot at it with wolf-tooth arrows; the boar ran several li.
translations.idiomatic: He went to Jing Mountain and shot the boar with wolf-tooth arrows; it ran several li.

sentences.zh: 大德十三年，進昭勇大將軍、臺州路達魯花赤。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year of Dade he was promoted to Grand General of Manifest Courage and darughachi of Taizhou Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year of Dade he was promoted to Grand General of Manifest Courage and darughachi of Taizhou Circuit.

sentences.zh: 卒，年八十一。

translations.literal: He died, aged eighty-one.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the age of eighty-one.

sentences.zh: 子不花，僉嶺南廣西道肅政廉訪司事；

translations.literal: His son Buhua was Commissioner of the Surveillance Commission for Integrity of the Lingnan and Guangxi Circuit;
translations.idiomatic: His son Buhua was Commissioner of the Surveillance Commission for Integrity of the Lingnan and Guangxi Circuit;

sentences.zh: 文圭，有隱德，贈秘書監著作郎；
